scope: five frozen feature inventories; other repository paths are covered by the complete file census, not asserted to be product features
measurement_warning: Raw feature LOC and predicted savings overlap and are not additive. No implementation savings have been measured.

features.name: Subcommand dispatch, help and usage text
features.description: Shared bash engine entry: raises the nofile limit, records the operator pid, then a 40-arm case statement routes every aiur/aiurdev subcommand; `help`/`-h`/`--help` print a hand-written usage block; an unknown word exits 64 (or runs if it is an existing path).
features.docs: website/docs-app/reference/cli.md (What the CLI does; Inspect and operate)
features.usage_evidence: Every invocation passes through it: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes) found 1,960 executor `aiurdev` + 365 executor `aiur` invocations and 327 + 1,258 agent ones. Explicit `--help`/`help`: 19 executor, 38 agent.
features.raw_rationale: The dispatch table, the usage block in the engine, Aiur.CLI.usage_message/0 and reference/cli.md are four hand-maintained copies of one command list. A 4,179-line bash program is the product front door, which makes every new command a bash+Elixir+docs triple edit.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Declare commands once (name, args, flags, handler, help) and generate dispatch, help and the docs table from it. Ship the CLI as a small client package separate from the daemon.

features.name: Run / attach session lifecycle (bare `aiur`, `aiur run`, `--bg`)
features.description: Starts the release inside a keyed tmux session (foreground TUI or detached headless), or attaches to this repository's live session; directory launch lock, per-instance record, argv tempfile handoff, startup wait for control-plane and dashboard readiness, foreground teardown traps and session cleanup; Elixir side parses argv, selects the config (positional path or discovery) and boots the app.
modules: packaging/npm/aiur-cli/libexec/aiur-engine.sh (run_session group 427: default_dashboard_host, build_run_argv, run_session, attach_tmux_session, resolve_tmux_conf; startup/probe/cleanup 261; instance record + launch lock 209; minus ~35 flag-handling lines counted under cli-03/cli-04)
features.docs: website/docs-app/reference/cli.md (Start, initialize, and queue); guide/quick-start.md; concepts/operating-aiur.md
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): `run` 45 executor (43 with --bg), bare run 79 executor / 219 agent (includes some `command -v aiur` noise), `--bg` first-token 8; restart re-enters this path 16 times. 40 run-log dirs in ~/.aiur/logs (2026-09-15..09-26) are one launch each. Human shell history: 1 bare `aiurdev` launch.
features.raw_rationale: Core, but most of the size is compensation for running a BEAM under a detached tmux with shell-side identity: launch-lock stale-owner recovery, instance-record adoption, attach-without-teardown-ownership, startup probing of epmd and the dashboard. Recurring fixes: #534 (startup failure exits 0), #592 (control command adopted another instance), #2362 (wrong checkout booted).
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Let the daemon own its lifecycle (pidfile + health endpoint, or a service manager); the CLI starts it, waits on one readiness URL, and attaches the TUI as a separate client. Keep the per-repository instance key.

features.name: Run flags that are used: --executor, --max-agents, --debug, --host, --port, --pause
features.description: Launch overrides: mark the run Executor-owned (roster principal, alert authority), session agent cap, verbose logs + chat-pane recording, dashboard bind host/port, cold start with the global pause on.
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes), flag counts on run/restart/--bg invocations (executor): --executor 61, --max-agents 57, --bg 62, --debug 38, --host 21, --port 21, --pause 11 (grep of Claude Executor Bash commands alone: --pause 4).
features.raw_rationale: Each is used by the Executor and is a one-line override of config.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Keep as plain overrides of config keys; --debug should just set log level + recorder.

features.name: Unused run flags: --interactive, --headless, --no-dashboard, --logs-root, guardrails acknowledgement switch
features.description: Mode flags the launcher injects itself (--interactive for foreground, --headless for --bg), a dashboard suppressor with Remote Control rejection, a per-launch log root override, and the mandatory `--i-understand-that-this-will-be-running-without-the-usual-guardrails` switch the launcher always inserts.
modules: packaging/npm/aiur-cli/libexec/aiur-engine.sh (build_run_argv injection, no_dashboard handling in run_session and print_dashboard_status: ~25)
features.docs: website/docs-app/reference/cli.md (Start table rows); AGENTS.md Running section
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): 0 operator-typed uses of --interactive, --headless, --no-dashboard, --logs-root in every population; confirmed by a second grep of Claude Executor Bash commands (0 each). The acknowledgement switch is only ever inserted by build_run_argv. AIUR_LOGS_ROOT env (used by the aiurdev agent sandbox) is independent of the flag.
features.raw_rationale: Nobody passes them. Foreground vs --bg already decides TUI vs headless; the guardrails switch is ceremony the launcher always satisfies; --no-dashboard needs special rejection logic for Remote Control.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Derive UI mode from --bg; keep AIUR_LOGS_ROOT env only if the dev sandbox needs it; drop the acknowledgement switch.

challenge.note: The five flags form different contracts and cannot be cut as one unused group. The launcher inserts --interactive and --headless internally, so zero operator-typed occurrences cannot establish dead code. --no-dashboard is a documented foreground and background mode with a Remote Control safety check in AGENTS.md and the CLI reference. --logs-root was used by the isolated 2026-09-29 native Muse acceptance to keep the test run separate from the shared daemon; that is observed post-snapshot use, not evidence of frozen-period frequency. The guardrails acknowledgement is launcher-injected, and removing it changes the daemon's accepted launch contract. Consolidate internal mode handling if equivalent tests prove it; preserve the documented operator flags and safety behavior. Any line saving must be measured after implementation. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

features.name: Control-command RPC transport (distribution identity, `bin/aiur rpc`, exit/error markers, 10s watchdog)
features.description: Every control command resolves the per-repository node name, cookie and tmux socket, spawns a second release BEAM running `bin/aiur rpc "Aiur.AgentControlCLI.<fn>(...)"`, kills it after 10 s, parses `__AIUR_CONTROL_EXIT__:`/`__AIUR_CONTROL_ERROR__:` markers from stdout, probes epmd to tell down from wedged, adopts a global-config instance record, and returns code 75 so aiurdev can rebuild and retry. Elixir side: `guarded/2`, timeout budgets, failure/crash formatting and the marker emitters in AgentControlCLI.
modules: packaging/npm/aiur-cli/libexec/aiur-engine.sh (identity/distribution 226: aiur_project_root, aiur_instance_key, aiur_resolve_identity, ensure_erlang_cookie, prepare_distribution, resolve_release, build_release_cmd; rpc transport 345: run_release_rpc_with_timeout, run_control_rpc(_dispatch), run_control_stream, marker parsing, elixir_list_literal, parse_issue_targets, encode_control_value)
src/lib/aiur/agent_control_cli.ex (shared helpers lines 1-97 and 3030-3408: guarded, control_query_timeout, report_control_query_failure, exit/error markers: 476)
features.docs: website/docs-app/reference/cli.md (Operational facts: bounded RPC, exit 124, crash marker)
features.usage_evidence: Carries every daemon command: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes) counted ~1,650 executor control invocations (status 647, agents 236, alerts 118, commands 113, github-cost 77, ...). Git: agent_control_cli.ex is the #2 hot file in fixes/merged-fixes.md (63 fix PRs of 86, 73% fix share); control-RPC latency recurred #698 -> #888 -> #2182 -> #2204 -> #2694 with #2519 open; silent failures #1684/#1736.
features.raw_rationale: Each command boots a full BEAM (~2 s, per the #1684 comment in agent_control_cli.ex) and speaks a stdout marker protocol through a shell watchdog. The daemon already serves an HTTP API (observability + decision controllers), so the transport duplicates a channel that exists.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: CLI = thin HTTP/JSON (or unix-socket) client of the daemon: one request per command, JSON response, exit code from HTTP status. Removes cookie/epmd/marker/watchdog code and the per-command BEAM start. Keep per-repository instance addressing (a port or socket path in the instance record).

features.name: aiur status
features.description: Daemon-wide report: fleet rows with status reasons, polling cadence/idle backoff, capacity binding and admission samples with age, GitHub quota measurement, build-gate holders, global pause banner, Executor listener/wake cursor, CODEOWNERS trust, CI readiness, supervision health, prewarm state, blocking asks.
modules: src/lib/aiur/agent_control_cli.ex (status/1, fleet view, print_status_report, print_status_table..print_load_status, print_global_pause_banner..tracker_state_sets: 810, minus 44 blocking-ask lines counted under cli-37)
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): 647 executor invocations (aiur 308, architecture-docs 240, khala 70, archon 29), 30 agent; plus the hourly aiur-run executor-cli-check.sh runs status/agents/alerts on every meta check (93 aiur + 22 archon meta logs; 236 Executor tool calls reference that script or executor-retrospective.sh). Referenced 15 times in skills.
features.raw_rationale: Most-used command, but it renders twelve subsystems with its own reason/label logic parallel to status_report.ex, waiting_reason.ex, `agents` and the dashboard; merged-fixes records the surfaces disagreeing (#1801 -> #2700 -> #2706 open).
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Render one server-side status projection (the same JSON the dashboard uses) with a generic table/record printer; absorb `usage` as a section.

features.name: aiur agents
features.description: One line per agent: state (including waiting_for_human cause) and current activity; the headless equivalent of the TUI agent list.
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): 236 executor invocations (aiur 125, archon 78, kevinweaver-dev 16, architecture-docs 10, khala 7), 8 agent; also run by the hourly executor-cli-check.sh.
features.raw_rationale: Core fleet view the Executor reads constantly; the natural merge target for `watch` and `units`.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Make it the single fleet table: add --changes (from watch), --json and unit filters (from units).

features.name: aiur watch (--full | --changes | --once | --interval)
features.description: Server-side status board: per-row state/activity/age, persistent-term baseline to print only changed rows, ACTIONABLE section (attention alerts, blocking asks, stuck > 600 s, PR-ready, removed rows); --interval re-renders.
modules: src/lib/aiur/agent_control_cli.ex (watch/1, print_watch_board, watch_row..print_orchestrator_status_error: 286, minus 9 ask lines counted under cli-37)
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): 19 executor invocations (all with --full; aiur 10, architecture-docs 9), last seen 2026-09-03; 0 agent. Skills still name `aiurdev watch` as the periodic tick (10 mentions; watch-alerts.sh).
features.raw_rationale: Duplicates `agents` (same rows, same activity) plus alert/ask lines that `alerts` and `status` already print. The skill calls it the backstop, but the Executor ran it 19 times vs 236 for `agents`.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Merge into `agents --changes`; the ACTIONABLE section becomes `alerts --needs-attention`.

challenge.note: `watch` reads the daemon fleet view without a GitHub round trip and adds a persistent delta baseline, removed-row detection, attention/ask evidence and an ACTIONABLE section; the monitor skill names `watch --full` its primary board and `--changes` its periodic tick. A lower invocation count than `agents` therefore does not establish duplicate behavior. Consolidation into `agents --changes` can hold only if the same server-side baseline, full/changes/interval modes, freshness and actionable signals survive, including restart-baseline handling. Count eliminated code after an output-equivalence test; 280 lines is a gross estimate. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

features.name: aiur alerts (--needs-attention)
features.description: Prints the structured alert feed (AlertFeed), optionally only unresolved needs-attention alerts; answered by a different process than the orchestrator, so it doubles as a liveness check.
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): 118 executor invocations, 104 of them with --needs-attention (aiur 77, architecture-docs 33, archon 8); also in every hourly executor-cli-check.sh run.
features.raw_rationale: Small and heavily used.

features.name: aiur usage (provider meter headroom)
features.description: Codex/Claude usage-limit windows from the provider meter projection, each with observation age and reset time; also `usage_bar/…` helpers.
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): 8 executor invocations (all aiur, 2026-08-22..09-09), 1 agent. Grep of Claude Executor Bash lines: 3 invoking, 10 mentions.
features.raw_rationale: Nine uses in ten weeks; the same meters appear on the dashboard and Stream Deck. A status section is enough.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Fold into `status` (provider headroom section) or `status --json`.

challenge.note: The low observed invocation count makes a dedicated usage command a reasonable consolidation candidate, but the output carries provider windows, observation age and reset time, including an explicit unknown state. A status section or JSON envelope must retain those fields and their source freshness; a dashboard or Stream Deck display does not by itself cover headless operators or script callers. Preserve documented `aiur usage` compatibility until callers can migrate, and measure the net deletion after adding the status presentation. The 80-line figure is predictive, not measured. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

features.name: aiur --todo <ids...> [--only]
features.description: Queues numeric tickets by adding agent:todo through the running daemon and requests a prompt poll; --only also removes agent:todo from other pending tickets (GitHub-only, <=50 targets, stops after 3 rate-limit failures). Aiur.CLI carries a second, unreachable parser for the same flags.
modules: src/lib/aiur/cli.ex (evaluate_todo/parse_todo_ids/run_todo_command: ~45; not reachable from the engine, which intercepts --todo)
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): 66 executor invocations (aiur 44, archon 11, architecture-docs 7, khala 4), 1 agent; `--only` 3 times.
features.raw_rationale: Queueing is core. --only is ~130 lines (plus tests) for 3 uses and is the open #2519 timeout; the Aiur.CLI todo branch is dead because the engine routes --todo to the control RPC.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Keep `aiur todo <ids>` (a subcommand, not a flag); drop --only and the second parser.

features.name: aiur set max-agents <n>
features.description: Changes the live session agent cap without editing config; warns when the orchestrator mailbox is backed up.
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): 13 executor invocations (aiur 8, khala 3, architecture-docs 2) plus 2 `set --help`.
features.raw_rationale: Small, used, and the only runtime knob.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Generalize to `aiur set <key> <value>` only if a second key appears.

features.name: aiur pause | resume (global switch and per-agent <ids|--all>)
features.description: Bare form flips the durable daemon-wide pause; with ids pauses at a safe boundary or resumes (reactivates deactivated/completed agents, starts idle eligible tickets), then polls each agent's control status for up to 4 s to confirm the resume actually applied, classifying queued/dropped/declined/superseded outcomes.
modules: src/lib/aiur/agent_control_cli.ex (pause/1, resume/1, pause_global, resume_global, set_global_pause*, control, control_status .. unknown_resume_detail, resume_confirm_timeout_ms: ~546)
features.docs: website/docs-app/reference/cli.md (pause/resume rows; Global pause is durable)
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): resume 58 executor (architecture-docs 21, aiur 18, khala 17), pause 17 executor, 3 agent. Memory note: "Aiur global pause survives restart — run bare aiurdev resume".
features.raw_rationale: Needed, but ~400 lines exist only because the orchestrator resume is asynchronous and the CLI must poll to avoid printing a false "resumed" (#1634). Pause/resume is area D in merged-fixes (13 fix PRs).
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Have the daemon return the settled outcome of a resume request (or a request id with a final state), and render it; drop CLI-side polling and outcome classification.

features.name: aiur reset-budget <ids>
features.description: Clears a ticket's lifetime dispatch-budget latch (#1453); rejects --all.
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): 3 executor invocations (aiur, 2026-08-23..08-24); grep check: 2 invoking Bash lines, 7 mentions. None since 08-24.
features.raw_rationale: A separate verb for one latch that `resume` explicitly cannot clear; used 3 times.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: `aiur resume <id> --reset-budget`, or remove the latch if the rewrite drops lifetime budgets.

challenge.note: The dispatch-budget latch is a distinct durable state. The CLI reference explicitly says resume cannot clear it, and the orchestrator has its own reset_dispatch_budget call path. Merging the spelling into `resume <id> --reset-budget` is plausible only if the implementation keeps an explicit per-ticket acknowledgement, rejects --all, preserves the latch reset transaction and documents that the flag changes two states. Do not remove the lifetime budget itself as an incidental simplification. The 35-line estimate is gross wrapper removal, not a measured net saving after parse/docs/tests. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

features.name: aiur message <id> [--message-id ID] <text>
features.description: Base64-transports Executor text to one agent's native queue, waits up to 1.5 s to report delivered vs queued, supports idempotent retry by message id, and prints the exact retry command on timeout.
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): 47 executor invocations (aiur 15, architecture-docs 13, kevinweaver-dev 11, archon 6, khala 2), 1 agent.
features.raw_rationale: The Executor's main way to steer a running agent; idempotency is justified by #2717.

features.name: aiur stop (agent-tree reap, workspace-cwd sweep, tmux/tmp sweeps)
features.description: Marks a clean stop, TERMs the BEAM with a long grace, reaps agent pid trees and processes rooted in the workspace root, backstops with node-name BEAM kills, sweeps dead tmux sockets and stale /tmp artifacts, and warns about other aiur daemons.
modules: packaging/npm/aiur-cli/libexec/aiur-engine.sh reaping helpers not claimed by subsystems-30 (kill_beams_matching, pid_*, agent_pid_tree, reap_aiur_agents, workspace_cwd_pids, reap_workspace_cwd_agents...: ~190 of 305)
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): 53 executor invocations (aiur 35, architecture-docs 17, archon 1), 1 agent; human history 1. restart runs the same path 16 more times.
features.raw_rationale: Needed, but process reaping recurred (#426/#458/#501 -> #2080 -> #2179 -> #2391 -> #2406 open, PID reuse). Bash reconstructs process ownership from /proc because the daemon does not own its children in a process group or cgroup.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Daemon spawns agents in its own process group/cgroup and kills the group on stop; CLI sends one stop request and waits. Drop tmp/tmux sweeps once nothing leaks.

features.name: aiur restart [--no-build] [run flags]
features.description: Stop, then (under aiurdev) run the deferred rebuild through AIUR_RESTART_BUILD_CMD, verify a build receipt/stamp names the expected checkout and commit, then start detached; refuses when the stopped daemon still answers; reports the stopped fleet on any failure.
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): 16 executor invocations (aiur 11, khala 3, archon 2) carrying --executor 16, --debug 12, --bg 11, --no-build 8 (grep: 13 --no-build Bash lines). Memory: restarting is pre-authorized and routine after merges.
features.raw_rationale: Useful, but the receipt/stamp verification protocol (and its 275 lines of aiurdev tests) exists to catch the wrong-checkout rebuild (#2362), which a cwd-targeted dev launcher removes.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: restart = stop; build (dev only, same checkout as cwd); start. No cross-process receipt.

features.name: aiur cleanup-stale [--dry-run] and stale manual-smoke inventory
features.description: Inventories orphaned manual-smoke BEAMs, wrapper tmux sockets and opencode attach processes left by `--test` runs; warns at startup, reaps on stop or on demand.
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): 1 executor invocation (architecture-docs, 2026-09-03), 0 agent; grep: 1 Bash line.
features.raw_rationale: Cleans up after a dev harness that agents are now blocked from running (aiurdev refuses --test in agent workspaces); one use in ten weeks.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: If the smoke harness survives (subsystems-36), give it its own teardown.

challenge.note: The agent-workspace --test guard blocks ticket workers from resetting pinned GitHub sandbox tickets; it does not remove Executor-root manual testing. AGENTS.md still requires the real foreground CLI/TUI smoke path, and the launcher calls preflight_stale_manual_smoke on foreground startup and reap_stale_manual_smoke on stop. The inventory uses same-user, workspace-path and tmux-aliveness checks before reaping stale BEAMs, plus orphan-attach and wrapper-socket checks. One explicit CLI use does not count automatic preflight/stop executions or the loss from abandoned child processes. Preserve scoped stale cleanup while the smoke harness exists; simplify inventory only after measuring false-positive/false-negative behavior, and keep dry-run visibility before destructive cleanup. The 181-line estimate is an unsupported net saving. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

features.name: Launcher dotenv credential loading
features.description: Loads ./.env then ~/.aiur/.env into unset names (blank = unset), treats GitHub credentials as one group from the first file that sets any, and scrubs run-only names (CI readiness token) before init.
modules: packaging/npm/aiur-cli/libexec/aiur-engine.sh load_dotenv, github_credential_env_name, parse_dotenv_line, dotenv_file_sets_github_credential, load_dotenv_file, scrub_run_only_env (81)
features.usage_evidence: Runs on every launch (every run/restart counted in cli-02/cli-17). The same precedence is implemented again in Aiur.Env.read_dotenv (src/lib/aiur/env.ex, config-36) and Aiur.Init.Dotenv (init/dotenv.ex).
features.raw_rationale: Third copy of one precedence rule (bash engine, Aiur.Env, Aiur.Init.Dotenv); #2638 shows the rule is subtle enough that copies drift.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Resolve credentials once in the daemon (config-36 Aiur.Env) and have the CLI pass nothing but cwd.

challenge.note: The three dotenv parsers can drift, and the GitHub credential group precedence is subtle (#2638), but moving all resolution into the daemon does not preserve the frozen launcher contract. `run_aiur` calls `load_dotenv` before it chooses `AIUR_DEFAULT_DASHBOARD_HOST`, starts the release, and scrubs the run-only CI readiness token; the launcher needs some credential presence before BEAM boot, and `aiur init` has its own pre-daemon use. Consolidate a shared parser or generated contract only after specifying this preboot boundary, preserving shell-export precedence, blank handling, GitHub-group isolation and child scrubbing. The raw 70-line saving is speculative until the replacement code and tests are counted. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

features.name: Legacy `.aiurconfig` rejection
features.description: Walks cwd/AIUR_REPO_ROOT/home for a legacy `.aiurconfig` and refuses to start with a pointer to `.aiur/config`; mirrored in Aiur.Workflow, Aiur.CLI and init.
features.usage_evidence: `find <local-home>/github/everdred ~ -maxdepth 4 -name .aiurconfig` returns nothing; the `.aiur/` folder replaced it on 2026-06-21 (#391/#392) and support was removed 2026-08-16 (#2023).
features.raw_rationale: A migration guard for a format no file on the host uses, three months after the rename.

challenge.note: A search that finds no `.aiurconfig` on the research host cannot measure installed users who still have one. The documented behavior deliberately rejects a legacy file with an actionable migration error, while config discovery otherwise falls through to `~/.aiur/config`. Removing that guard risks silently running a different workflow for a user who expected the local legacy file to apply. The 134-line gross estimate is too small to justify a compatibility break without a measured installed population and an equivalent fail-closed detection path. Keep the migration guard or replace it with a smaller equivalent; test local and global discovery precedence. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

features.name: aiur --version and dispatcher/release version-skew warning
features.description: Prints release version + git rev + npm dispatcher version without claiming the node; on an unknown subcommand compares the dispatcher package version with the checkout's and says to update aiur-cli.
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): 5 executor (architecture-docs 3, khala 2), 20 agent (khala 11, aiur 6).
features.raw_rationale: --version is cheap and used; the skew diagnosis exists because the npm dispatcher and the release ship separately.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Ship the CLI and release as one versioned artifact; keep plain --version.

features.name: aiur upgrade [--force]
features.description: Detects npm/bun/Homebrew/dev install method, refuses under aiurdev, Homebrew or a running daemon (unless --force), and installs the newer aiur-cli on the user's channel (latest/next/nightly) without downgrading.
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): 0 invocations in every population (grep of Claude Executor transcripts: 5 mentions in Write/Bash text, 0 invoking). The host's global npm aiur-cli is 0.0.3 while packaging/npm/aiur-cli/package.json is 0.0.5, i.e. never upgraded; the operator runs aiurdev (1,960 executor invocations vs 365 for aiur).
features.raw_rationale: No use; `npm i -g aiur-cli@<channel>` does the same. The channel-comparison logic is the part that breaks.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Document the npm command; drop the subcommand and the in-daemon registry check (subsystems-37).

challenge.note: The proposed `npm i -g aiur-cli@<channel>` does not do everything the frozen command does. `cmd_upgrade` detects dev/Brew/unknown installs, refuses a live daemon unless --force, derives latest/next/nightly from installed version and registry tags, avoids downgrade, and explains restart behavior. Zero observed invocations and a stale global npm install support low priority, not equivalence of a raw npm command; installed-user use is not measured by Executor transcripts. Simplify or remove only with an explicit package-manager replacement and documented stop/channel/restart safety contract, then count actual removed lines. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

features.name: aiur init [--force] (CLI entry)
features.description: Distribution-free boot of the release into Aiur.Init (interactive wizard); `--force` recreates generated files. The wizard itself is inventoried as subsystems-38.
modules: packaging/npm/aiur-cli/libexec/aiur-engine.sh run_init (9; build_init_cmd is counted in cli-05)
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): 2 executor + 7 agent invocations; human ~/.zsh_history (281 lines, 41 containing "aiur"): 4 `aiurdev init` lines. 5 non-worktree repo configs exist (aiur, archon, kevinweaver-dev, 2 private) plus ~/.aiur/config.
features.raw_rationale: First-run entry is required for adoption; the size problem is inside the wizard (subsystems-38).

features.name: aiur units (--scope, --condition, --format, --json)
features.description: Terminal form of the Dashboard Units page: filtered unit catalog with scope/condition filters, auto/table/records layout and the versioned JSON envelope.
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): 13 executor invocations (architecture-docs 11, aiur 2; --scope 10, --format 9), 2 agent; last 2026-09-10.
features.raw_rationale: Fourth fleet view beside status, agents and watch; 13 uses vs 236 for agents.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Serve units as `agents --json` with filters from the same server projection the dashboard uses.

challenge.note: `aiur units` is a filtered catalog over current-run membership, including non-running tickets; the launcher and UnitsCLI share the Dashboard Units projection with scope, condition, format, source freshness and a versioned JSON envelope. `agents` and `watch` are active-agent fleet views and cannot express the non-running catalog. Thirteen observed Executor calls are a real population, not zero. A common CLI umbrella could reuse presentation code, but replacing Units with `agents --json` would need its own catalog query and schema, likely moving rather than deleting most lines. Retain the distinct query contract until equivalent output and net physical deletion are demonstrated. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

Executor also read decisions by direct RPC 13 times (Aiur.DecisionStore.get).

The Executor also answered by direct RPC Aiur.DecisionStore.answer 9 times (memory note "use DecisionStore.answer via RPC").

features.name: aiur build-orders [root] [--json]

features.name: aiur analytics (--range, --since, --until, --build-order, --json)
features.description: Terminal form of the Analytics page: fleet/build pressure peaks, binding admission signal, longest build wait, timestamped series in JSON. Renderer analytics_cli.ex is inventoried under subsystems-02.
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): 0 invocations in every population. A second grep of Claude Executor tool_use lines found 13 textual mentions (Write 4, Bash text 6, Agent/SendMessage/StructuredOutput 3), none invoking.
features.raw_rationale: Never run; the dashboard page and run-telemetry reports cover the need.

challenge.note: The documented terminal analytics form supplies a selectable retained time window, Build Order scope and a timestamped JSON pressure series; the dashboard capture skill explicitly calls the /analytics page current data, not a frozen window. Zero invocations in the sampled transcript population does not prove that this read-only diagnostic contract has no other headless consumer. A cut would need a counted installed/API population and a replacement query that preserves source freshness, unavailable/null semantics and historical time filters. The raw 45-line estimate omits the renderer owned under subsystems-02 and does not establish meaningful net deletion. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

features.name: aiur github-cost (--budget graphql|core|all, --format, --json)
features.description: Ranks GitHub API spend by call site in points and points/hour with credential-window reconciliation, from the daemon's meter (no GitHub request). Renderer github_cost_cli.ex is inventoried under integrations-18.
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): 77 executor (aiur 76, khala 1; --budget 24, --format 6, --json 6), 4 agent. AGENTS.md makes it the required measurement for saving claims.
features.raw_rationale: Used, and required by the saving-claim rule in AGENTS.md.

features.name: aiur github-usage [--json]
features.description: Per-actor (daemon vs each agent workspace) Core/GraphQL/search used/limit from the admission broker. Renderer github_usage_cli.ex is inventoried under integrations-18.
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): 14 executor (khala 7, aiur 4, architecture-docs 3).
features.raw_rationale: A second GitHub-budget view beside github-cost; 14 uses vs 77.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: `github-cost --by actor` (merge target: cli-29).

challenge.note: `github-usage` reports per-actor and per-credential Core, GraphQL and search request-count ceilings with reset windows; `github-cost` attributes Core/GraphQL points to call sites and reconciles a separate credential window. The GitHub API documentation and both CLI contracts warn against treating these as one metric. A common command family could present both only with distinct named schemas, units, windows and 0-versus-unknown states; changing the spelling saves about 26 wrapper lines at most while risking operator confusion. Keep the separate query contract until a measured demand and migration plan justify consolidation. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

features.name: aiur executor-wait (--timeout, --json, --as)
features.description: Blocks until durable Executor wake records are pending (or times out quietly), auto-claims the wake stream, renews the lease while blocking, acknowledges for the owner, and reports stage-specific exit codes (0/1/64/69).
features.docs: website/docs-app/reference/cli.md (executor-wait outcomes; Wake ledger bound and lease TTL)
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): 67 executor invocations (architecture-docs 34, aiur 28, khala 3, archon 2), 66 with --json --timeout. Competing path: 297 Executor tool_use lines reference `executor.wakes.ndjson` (aiur 140, khala 79, archon 56, architecture-docs 22), i.e. tail -F/Monitor on the wake file.
features.raw_rationale: The supported consumption path for wakes; used regularly even though the Executor more often tails the file.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Keep; make it the only consumer path so the file-tail workaround is unnecessary.

features.name: aiur executor-fast-forward <wake-id> [--as]
features.description: Recovery command: acknowledges an exact durable wake prefix already covered by other means, refusing a live peer owner.
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): 0 invocations; grep of Claude Executor transcripts: 1 textual mention, 0 invoking.
features.raw_rationale: Never used; executor-wait already consumes and acknowledges.

challenge.note: `executor-fast-forward` is an exceptional repair for a wake prefix already covered by another complete means. `.claude/skills/aiur-run/SKILL.md` and the CLI reference specify owner-lease checks, exact-prefix acknowledgement and preservation of newer wakes. Zero normal invocations is expected for an emergency recovery command and does not prove the recovery path is redundant with `executor-wait`, which acknowledges only its own successful consumption. Keep the capability unless an equivalent bounded recovery route is designed and tested. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

features.name: aiur executor-roster [--json]
features.description: Lists Executor consumers with evidence-derived state (active/idle/stalled/expired/unknown), lease times, cursor and pending count.
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): 8 executor invocations (aiur 4, architecture-docs 3, archon 1; 2 with --json), 2026-09-02..09-20.
features.raw_rationale: Small read-only diagnostic for the multi-Executor claim model; keep while that model exists.

features.name: aiur executor-claim | executor-release | executor-revoke
features.description: Explicit wake-stream lease management: claim (refused when a live owner renews), release, and operator-only revoke of a named owner.
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): 0 invocations of all three; grep of Claude Executor transcripts: executor-claim 0, executor-release 1 textual mention, executor-revoke 0.
features.raw_rationale: executor-wait auto-claims and leases expire on their own (10-minute TTL); the manual verbs were never used.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Keep claim/release semantics inside executor-wait; expose revoke only if a real takeover incident appears.

challenge.note: Automatic claims and lease expiry do not replace all manual authority transitions. `.claude/skills/aiur-run/SKILL.md` treats `executor-revoke` as an operator decision after roster evidence and expressly forbids an agent from revoking a live peer itself. `executor-release` permits immediate handoff instead of waiting for TTL; claim refusal makes ownership visible. The zero-use sample is not a safe reason to remove these incident controls. Preserve them behind explicit owner/authority checks, or design and prove an equivalent takeover contract before removing a verb. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

features.name: aiur executor-listen | executor-emit | executor-subscribe | executor-unsubscribe | executor-subscriptions
features.description: Executor half of the message bus from the terminal: stream persisted-pattern events as JSON lines (bypassing the RPC timeout), publish on `executor.*`, and manage persistent topic bindings.
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): 0 invocations of all five in every population; grep of Claude Executor transcripts: executor-listen 0, executor-emit 0, executor-subscribe 1 (Write text), executor-unsubscribe 0, executor-subscriptions 0.
features.raw_rationale: The Executor consumes wakes through executor-wait or by tailing the wake file; the streaming/bus verbs were never used.

challenge.note: The five commands combine an optional raw stream with persistent event-bus administration. `.claude/skills/aiur-run/SKILL.md` says `executor-listen` is optional, not obsolete, and describes `executor-emit` plus binding management for general Executor coordination; the CLI reference defines validated topic patterns. The zero invocation window does not measure all external operators or incident use. Consolidate the admin surface if the same event authority, replay, scope validation and observable receipts survive; do not delete the entire group based on a normal-loop usage count. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

features.name: aiur findings (CLI entry: read, --record, --digest)
features.description: Distribution-free boot into FindingsCLI: read the host-local findings ledger (--unfiled, --slugs, --scope), append one validated record (--record --repo), or render the Markdown digest. Ledger and renderer are inventoried under integrations-40.
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): 10 executor (8 with --record), 7 agent. Ledgers: `wc -l ~/.aiur/repo/*/*/meta/findings.ndjson` = 73 records (aiur 43, khala 13, kevinweaver-dev 9, archon 8; private 0; plus empty test-pollution dirs acme/widgets, owner/repo, test-org/test-repo).
features.raw_rationale: Executor bookkeeping for the aiur-meta skill, not orchestration; follows integrations-40.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: A skill-owned script appending NDJSON; remove the subcommand from the daemon CLI.

challenge.note: The finding ledger is host-local Executor/meta bookkeeping with 73 sampled records and a documented aiur-meta workflow, so an independently versioned skill-owned tool is a plausible owner. Extraction must preserve repository state-node discovery, bounded record validation, append semantics, unfiled/latest-slug reduction, digest output and readable corrupt-record diagnostics. The existing `aiur findings` command is documented and used; ship a migration command and references before removing it. Moving the ledger/parser code is relocation, while only the thin CLI glue can count as net deletion after measurement. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

features.name: aiur ask | aiur asks (CLI entry + blocking-ask lines in status/watch)
features.description: Create/resolve durable operator requests for the current repository (--body/--body-file, --urgency, --blocking, --done/--note) and list them (--open/--all/--json); status and watch print open blocking asks. Store inventoried under integrations-39.
modules: src/lib/aiur/cli.ex ask parsing (evaluate_ask*, evaluate_asks, ask_body, ask_urgency, run_asks_command: ~64)
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): 0 executor invocations of ask or asks, 3 agent `ask` (aiur, 2026-08-12). Ledgers: 5 records total (aiur 5; archon, architecture-docs, khala and private 0).
features.raw_rationale: Five records since 2026-08-09; Decisions/Commands already model a blocking question with delivery. Merge target: `aiur commands` / DecisionStore (as integrations-39 proposes).

challenge.note: Asks are Executor-authored repository-operator requests with urgency, blocking, append-only resolution and notes. Commands are agent-originated decisions with offered options, optimistic versions, supersede/moot and ticket delivery. Their low-count ledgers do not make their authority and delivery contracts interchangeable. A shared presentation or notification layer may simplify status/watch, but moving asks into DecisionStore needs an explicit schema, authorization and migration design that preserves old ask history and does not send an operator-only request to an agent. The 120-line CLI estimate omits the store and migration cost. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

features.name: aiur guard-pr-deletions [base-branch]
features.description: Refuses a PR that deletes more than 50 files the branch never touched (exit 1), or has an unusable input (exit 2); agents run it before every push per the prompt builder.
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): 982 agent invocations (khala 556, aiur 202, architecture-docs 113, archon 83, <private repo> (private) (private) 28), 2026-08-11..09-26; 6 executor.
features.raw_rationale: Most-invoked command of the whole CLI, 79 lines, no daemon dependency.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Could live in an agent-tools package with the other pre-PR gates, but keep the behaviour unchanged.

features.name: Release rpc/eval escape hatch (`<release>/bin/aiur rpc` into internals)
features.description: Not an Aiur command: the Mix release's built-in rpc/eval, used by the Executor to call internal functions directly when the CLI lacks a verb.
modules: (mix release boot script; no Aiur code)
features.usage_evidence: rpc_mix_scan.py: 242 executor tool calls ran `bin/aiur rpc|eval` (2 agent). Named targets: Aiur.BuildOrder.GraphProjection.* 80 (catalog 34, refresh 15, refresh_catalog 14, selected 8, demand 5, read 1), Aiur.GitHub.ResourceStore.* 74 (key 22, drop_etag 16, drop_data 16, etag 6, data 5, list 4), Aiur.DecisionStore.* 29 (get 13, answer 9, retry_dispatch 3), GitHub.Quota.snapshot 6, Client.hydrate_blocked_by 6, Config.settings! 5, AgentQueueStore.get 5, Orchestrator.request_refresh 3, terminate_running_issue 3.
features.raw_rationale: Keep as break-glass, but the counts are a gap list: Build Order refresh, GitHub cache invalidation (the stale blocked_by bug), decision answer/retry and queue inspection had no supported verb.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Add supported commands (or fix the causes) for Build Order refresh, cache drop per key, decision retry-dispatch, and agent queue inspection.

features.name: aiur __identity (internal)
features.description: Prints the resolved instance identity (session prefix, instance key, node) for tooling.
features.usage_evidence: Run by executor-cli-check.sh on every hourly meta check (93 aiur + 22 archon meta logs); usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): 2 direct executor + 1 agent.
features.raw_rationale: 15 lines that let skills address the right instance.

features.name: npm distribution: aiur.js launcher, postinstall provisioning, platform packages, release packaging scripts
features.description: `aiur-cli` npm package: bin/aiur.js resolves the platform package's OTP release and lazily provisions tmux (>=3.3) and the pinned opencode (mirroring postinstall.mjs because bun/pnpm skip postinstall), verify-install.sh, and packaging/scripts to assemble/stamp/check platform packages.
features.usage_evidence: Host has global npm aiur-cli 0.0.3 (package.json in snapshot: 0.0.5). usage_scan binary counts: executor `aiur` 365 vs `aiurdev` 1,960; per-repo grep of Claude Executor tool lines for control verbs: aiur 60 vs aiurdev 1,413 (aiur 43/812, archon 16/155, architecture-docs 1/302, khala 0/144). External installs: unknown (npm download stats not queried).
features.raw_rationale: Needed to ship to anyone but the author, yet the operator himself runs dev builds; aiur.js deliberately duplicates postinstall provisioning.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: One provisioning path (first-run check in the launcher), no postinstall mirror; if the CLI becomes a thin HTTP client it can ship as its own small package.

features.name: aiurdev dev shim core (build-if-stale, build lock, build stamp, control release reuse + retry, `aiurdev build [--deps]`, setup)
features.description: Runs the shared engine against the checkout's `_build/dev/rel/aiur`, rebuilding when sources are newer or the stamp names another commit, serializing rebuilds with a directory lock, reusing a complete release for pure control commands and retrying once on exit 75, pinning opencode, capping agent mix schedulers (AIUR_AGENT_MIX_SCHEDULERS); scripts/setup installs mise and symlinks aiurdev.
modules: scripts/aiurdev (~442 of 912: header, require_mise, ensure_pinned_opencode, deps/build/stamp/lock, release_ready, ensure_built*, pure_control_command, ensure_control_surface, build command, exec + retry)
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): `aiurdev` 1,960 executor and 327 agent invocations; `build` 45 executor + 19 agent; --deps 0. Human history: 2 `aiurdev build`, 1 stop, 1 --debug, 4 init.
features.raw_rationale: The operator's real launcher across all repos. The stamp/lock/retry machinery exists because a control command and a rebuild can race on one release directory.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Build to a versioned directory and switch a symlink atomically (no lock, no exit-75 retry); a plain `mix` task can replace most of the shim.

features.name: aiurdev checkout targeting (script-path vs cwd divergence refusal)
features.description: Resolves the target checkout from the script path (following symlinks), and when cwd is inside a different aiur checkout refuses build/restart/run (exit 64) while letting control commands through without rebuilding; AIUR_REPO_ROOT overrides.
features.usage_evidence: Runs on every aiurdev invocation (1,960 executor + 327 agent). Added for #2362 (a rebuild shipped from a tree the operator never touched); memory notes "aiurdev AIUR_REPO_ROOT hazard" and "aiurdev vs aiur" record further incidents.
features.raw_rationale: The hazard comes from resolving the target from the script path; resolving it from cwd (like git or mix) removes the divergence case.

features.name: aiurdev manual smoke harness: --test, --test3, --clear, --allow-remote, test3 timer and phases
features.description: Dev-only flags: stop the keyed daemon, reset GitHub sandbox tickets (mix aiur.test.reset, subsystems-36), wait for the label index, optionally wipe ~/.aiur/logs, start a detached test3 wall-clock timer, and hand off to a foreground run; phases script extracts per-ticket timings.
modules: scripts/aiurdev (flag loop, --clear, test reset, label settle, test3 timer launch: ~155)
features.usage_evidence: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes): --test 9 agent (2026-08-09..08-17, 7 with --allow-remote) + 3 executor (last 2026-08-12); --test3 0; explicit --clear 0. AGENTS.md mandates `aiurdev --test` for manual testing, but no run since 2026-08-17 in the transcript window.
features.raw_rationale: A dev harness inside the product launcher; --test3 and its timer/phases were never used; agents are now blocked from running it at all.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Move the sandbox reset + smoke launch into a dev script next to the sandbox fixtures (subsystems-36); drop --test3, timer, phases and --clear.

challenge.note: The dev-only sandbox reset and timer belong beside the test fixtures rather than in the shared product launcher, but Executor-root aiurdev --test remains the canonical real CLI/TUI acceptance path in AGENTS.md; only agent-workspace launches are blocked. An extraction must preserve a one-command foreground path that starts the actual release and tmux, preserves --allow-remote safety, explicit force/clear semantics and cleanup, and keeps the user-facing CLI guide accurate. --test3 has no observed invocations in the sample, which supports prioritizing its removal after checking the three-ticket scenario owner; it does not prove that --test can be deleted. The 300-line figure is gross source movement/deletion; count retained harness lines as relocation and run manual acceptance on the extracted command. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

features.name: aiurdev agent IR sandbox
features.description: When aiurdev runs inside an agent workspace it redirects state, cookie, profiles, XDG dirs and logs into `<workspace>/.aiur-agent-ir` so an agent cannot address or clobber the operator's live daemon, and blocks --test/--test3 there.
features.usage_evidence: Applies to every agent aiurdev call: usage_scan.py (Executor + agent tool calls; method and window in coverage_notes) counted 327 agent `aiurdev` invocations (e.g. build 19, --help 34, status 30, --test 9).
features.raw_rationale: Cheap isolation that protects the live fleet from its own agents.

features.name: Launcher tmux configuration (two diverged copies) and Ctrl+C bridge
features.description: share/aiur.tmux.conf is what the engine loads; scripts/aiur.tmux.conf is an older diverged copy (extra terminal-features line and C-q binding) read only by verify-ctrlc-binding.sh; aiur-pane-ctrlc bridges Ctrl+C in opencode panes.
features.usage_evidence: Loaded by every foreground/background session (40 run dirs 2026-09-15..09-26). `diff` of the two confs (comments stripped) shows divergence; grep finds scripts/aiur.tmux.conf referenced only by scripts/verify-ctrlc-binding.sh, a comment in pane_manager/anchor.ex, and executor-retrospective.sh.
features.raw_rationale: Two copies of one config have already drifted, and the regression harness tests the copy the product does not load. Merge target: packaging/npm/aiur-cli/share/aiur.tmux.conf.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: One conf; point verify-ctrlc-binding.sh at it (or drop it if the TUI surface cuts the opencode panes, integrations-11).

challenge.note: The default launcher resolves the packaged share/aiur.tmux.conf after optional AIUR_TMUX_CONF and user configuration, while scripts/verify-ctrlc-binding.sh tests scripts/aiur.tmux.conf. The two tracked copies differ materially: the test copy has synchronized-output advertising and a C-q hide binding, and the packaged copy retains the old h=...; $h form that the regression harness comment says raw-kills a pane on Ctrl+C. The source comparison is a strong defect signal, but no live packaged-keypress reproduction is claimed here. Merge the files by choosing one tested packaged source, then run the real wrapper-client keypress regression against that exact file and test C-c, C-q and user override precedence. The 109-line estimate is gross deletion only; a retained regression test and comments count toward net LOC. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

features.name: Config loading, discovery, hot reload and accessor facade
features.description: Discovers ./.aiur/config then ~/.aiur/config, parses YAML, resolves sibling files (prompt_file, hooks_file, prewarm.base_build_file, alerts.alerts_file), normalizes legacy/alias sections (top-level linear: merged, root codex: rejected, top-level <backend>: and agent.<backend>: folded into agent.backend_configs, top-level github:/linear:/memory: infer tracker.kind, polling.interval_ms rejected), casts through the Ecto embedded schema, resolves $VAR secrets, caches in ETS via WorkflowStore (1s poll hot reload), and exposes ~114 public accessor functions in Aiur.Config. GlobalConfigStartup bootstraps labels when the global config is used.
features.usage_evidence: Real-config scan (22 distinct files: 7 current incl. 2 private + 15 historical; flatten.rb/usage_matrix.tsv, see coverage_notes): prompt_file set in 7/7 current (6 non-default), hooks_file 7/7. Executor transcripts (~/.claude/projects/-home-user-github-everdred-*/*.jsonl, python scan scratch-config/edits.py): 27 Edit tool calls on */.aiur/config (15 aiur, 12 architecture-docs). git log at 3339b88: config.ex 68 commits, config/schema.ex 45, reference doc 99; fixes/merged-fixes.md ranks config.ex #6 hot file (38 fix PRs of 72). The agent.<backend> shorthand is live in 2/7 current configs (global, config.archon: agent.deepseek.enabled) and in the snapshot's tracked aiur config, but appears nowhere in reference/configuration.md.
features.raw_rationale: Loading is core and must stay, but the layer is over-built: a 1,462-line facade of ~114 accessors that mostly re-read one struct field; five spellings for backend settings (agent.claude, agent.backend_configs.claude, agent.claude shorthand, top-level claude:, registry default); and unknown keys are silently dropped by Ecto cast (a typo like max_concurent_agents is accepted and ignored; the docs call this deliberate for removed keys). Config churn is high (38 fix PRs).
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Keep: discovery order, YAML + sibling-file resolution, $VAR resolution, ETS-cached hot reload. Remove: the per-field accessor functions (read the typed struct), all legacy/alias section folding (one canonical path per setting), GlobalConfigStartup (move label bootstrap to the GitHub package). Add: strict unknown-key rejection with a did-you-mean, and per-package schema registration (each feature package contributes its section) as codebase/feature-boundaries.md proposes.

features.name: TUI pane and opencode keys
features.description: Top-level max_vertical_panes and pre_warmed_sessions plus the opencode.* section (command, bridge_port, bridge_host, serve_args, model_prefix, prewarm_disabled) that drive the tmux/opencode chat-pane TUI. Aiur.Opencode.Config also reads opencode.db_path and opencode.prewarm_workspace, which are not schema fields.
features.usage_evidence: Real-config scan (22 distinct files: 7 current incl. 2 private + 15 historical; flatten.rb/usage_matrix.tsv, see coverage_notes): max_vertical_panes set 6/7, all at default 3 (0 non-default in 22 files). pre_warmed_sessions 7/7 set, 2 non-default (archon, kevinweaver-dev). opencode section set only in aiur (1/7), every value equal to its default; bridge_port and prewarm_disabled 0/22. opencode.db_path/prewarm_workspace: Opencode.Config.section_value/1 reads them from Aiur.Config.settings!().opencode, a struct with no such field, so they always resolve to nil; they are in no config and no doc.
features.raw_rationale: The pane count is the only key operators set away from default. The opencode section is copied at defaults, and two readers target keys the schema cannot hold (implemented-but-unreachable).
features.raw_rewrite_notes: If the TUI survives the rewrite, keep one pane-count key and pre_warmed_sessions; hardcode opencode command/bridge/model_prefix (env override for bridge port already exists as AIUR_OPENCODE_BRIDGE_PORT). Delete db_path/prewarm_workspace readers. If the opencode TUI (8,544 lib lines in src/lib/aiur/opencode, owned by the TUI surface) is cut, all of these go.

features.name: Log history cap (max_log_history_mb)
features.description: Top-level max_log_history_mb bounds ~/.aiur/logs; Aiur.Logs.Retention sweeps oldest sessions every 5 minutes once exceeded.
features.usage_evidence: Real-config scan (22 distinct files: 7 current incl. 2 private + 15 historical; flatten.rb/usage_matrix.tsv, see coverage_notes): set in 2/7 current (aiur at default, kevinweaver-dev non-default); 5 historical aiur versions at default. ~/.aiur/logs held 40 run directories / 865 MB on 2026-09-26 (research README), so the cap is active at default.

challenge.note:
The facts in the entry mostly check out. The merge rationale does not, because it treats two different scopes as one kind of knob. Keep the mechanism and fix its scope. Do not fold it into the per-repo observability section.

What checks out:
- LOC: retention.ex is 190 lines. The key adds about 8 lines (schema.ex:43/147/157, config.ex:597-600). Tests are 96 lines in retention_test.exs, plus about 15 in workspace_and_config_test.exs:2440.
- Usage: in the 7 current configs, the key is set in aiur (1000) and kevinweaver-dev (500). <private repo> (private) and <private repo> (private) have it commented out. archon does not have it. About 40 sibling and worktree clones of the aiur config also set it to 1000.
- The sweep is live. ~/.aiur/logs holds 39 dirs / 882 MB today. The aiur.log in 20260917T022859Z-1671510 records 2 `aiur_logs_retention phase=reap` deletions of about 43 MB each. The older evidence was deleted by the same sweep.
- Hidden consumer: `mix aiur.telemetry.dashboard` reads ~/.aiur/logs across sessions (aiur.telemetry.dashboard.ex:26/96). So this cap already limits how far back telemetry history reaches. That favours presenting the retention keys together.
- The test suite is safe: config.exs points HOME at a temp dir before the app boots.

Why "merge into config-25" is wrong:
1. **Different scopes.** telemetry_retention_* prunes one telemetry.ndjson inside the current launch's log dir. max_log_history_mb deletes whole session dirs from ~/.aiur/logs, which every repo and every instance shares (aiur-engine.sh:872 mints ~/.aiur/logs/<ts>-<pid> for any repo). But the key is read from the per-repo config. GlobalConfigStartup uses ~/.aiur/config only when a repo has no config of its own, so there is no layering.
2. **Existing bug that the merge would carry forward.** Each daemon starts its own Aiur.Logs.Retention (aiur.ex:459). Each one sweeps the shared root with its own repo's cap and protects only its own session (current_session_dir). A session dir's only child is `log/`, so its mtime stays at launch time. That makes a long-running live daemon's session the oldest candidate for another daemon's sweep. Concurrent daemons are real: census/runs.csv has 38 overlapping pairs across repos, for example <private repo> (private) 144h alongside aiur 133h and khala 62h. With the smallest cap in force, a kevinweaver-dev daemon at 500 MB would delete other repos' history, including live sessions. So the moduledoc's promise that "the active session is never deleted" holds only within one daemon, not across daemons. I did not observe a live session being deleted, because the evidence is gone, but the code path is there.
3. **Renaming risk.** Unknown top-level keys are silently ignored (only polling.ex:85 rejects unknown keys). A plain rename would quietly reset kevinweaver-dev from 500 back to 1000.

Rewrite: keep the sweeper (it is the documented replacement for LogFile rotation). Make the cap host-scoped with a single owner, or have every sweep protect all live sessions (by instance lock or pid). If keys are grouped under `retention:`, label the scope of each key. Give removed keys an actionable error. The claimed saving of about 20 LOC is right: the merge removes none of the 190-line mechanism.

challenge.note:
The recommendation is right that nobody uses the pool. It is wrong that the listed modules can be cut. Most of the 1,623 lines also serve the single-credential path, which every real install uses.

USAGE (the brief's finding stands): a list under `credentials:` appears in no real config. I checked ~/.aiur/config and all 13 .aiur/config files under <local-checkouts>/everdred. No token_env, app_installation or machine_user key appears in any config. Transcripts mention the key only where someone read configuration.md or during this research. So the pool feature itself (the 7 `tracker.github.credentials.*` keys and multi-credential selection) is dead.

WHAT A WHOLESALE CUT WOULD BREAK (single-credential, in production):
1. Broker ledger across App token rotation (#2268, commit 180ed2b2b, plan R4/KTD3). The single-credential branch of CredentialSelector.assign/2 attaches `credential_key = Credential.identity_key(legacy)`. Budget passes it to the broker as `--identity-key` (budget.ex:522, :759). resolve_credential_identity in priv/github_budget.py then maps each rotated App token back to one ledger. Without it, every hourly token rotation starts a new ledger and resets per-actor admissions and holds. Evidence of live use: ~/.aiur/github-budget/budget.sqlite3 has 5 credential_bindings rows, 2 of them identity==token (adopted ledgers).
2. The agent gh guard budget identity. agent_environment.ex:472-486 builds AIUR_GITHUB_BUDGET_IDENTITY_KEY from Credential.identity_key.
3. The CredentialHeadroom GenServer. It is in the supervision tree (aiur.ex:336) and observes every response (transport.ex:492). Budget uses it to raise system.github.budget_meter_disagreement (budget.ex:407-423). That alert is the safety signal for "local guard holds the fleet while GitHub reports headroom". No alert has fired in the ~/.aiur logs, but the path is live.
4. The GitHub cache dashboard page (#2315). It renders a per-credential identity meter for the single primary credential through BudgetMap.identity_meters -> CredentialSelector.headroom -> CredentialRegistry.legacy_credential + CredentialHeadroom.
5. ci_readiness (#2515). It uses the `credential_pinned?` assign branch and Credential.token_type.

LOC ATTRIBUTION IS WRONG: the sum of 1,623 is correct, but budget_map.ex (510 lines) is the live budget map for the cache page: caller ranking, free/billed/wasted verdicts, admissions, read cache, ResourceStore, webhooks and agent cache. Only identity_meters (about 20 lines) touches credentials. CredentialHeadroom (298) and Credential's stable identity are core accounting, not pool code. Of the 1,109 test lines, budget_map_test (254) is not pool coverage.

The truly pool-only code is about 550-600 lines. It includes:
- the GithubCredential schema (79) and the embeds_many/unique-id validation in tracker.ex (~20)
- in the registry: configured_entries, from_schema, warn_once, pooled?, by_id and by_token_key (~90)
- in the selector: choose, select, best, pick, score, intent, graphql_intent, fallback and apply_credential (~170)
- in Credential: eligible?, describe and the token_env path
- CredentialUsage.pool and the >=2-row credential views in github_usage_cli and github_cost_cli (these views show nothing with one credential)

Cutting this code also means removing its docs: 7 keys in configuration.md (check-config-docs.py enforces them) and the "Credential pooling" section of apis/github.md.

Recommended action: SIMPLIFY. Drop the config key and the multi-credential selection and pool reporting. Keep one small "credential identity" unit: the legacy credential, stable_identity/identity_key, assign-with-identity (including pinned), CredentialHeadroom and the budget-meter alert. Move BudgetMap to the cache-page feature.

challenge.note:
I could not refute the usage claim: nobody really uses Linear. But "externalize" is the wrong action, and the LOC and module attribution are materially understated.

USAGE (checked, none found): I scanned 70 .aiur/config files. That covers ~/.aiur/config and its 13 backups, every repo and worktree under <local-checkouts>/everdred/*, archon, kevinweaver-dev, and one private repo. Public configs use the GitHub tracker; the private source contributes only an aggregate count of no active Linear tracker use. None has a tracker.linear block or a top-level linear: section. The Executor transcripts in ~/.claude/projects have 0 tool_use calls to any linear tool.

NEW EVIDENCE the author missed: DynamicTool.LinearGraphQL (src/lib/aiur/codex/dynamic_tool.ex @handlers) is offered to every Codex agent, whatever the tracker kind. Across 344 agent.ndjson files under ~/code/aiur-workspaces, agents on the GitHub-tracked aiur-team/aiur run made 56 linear_graphql calls between 2026-07-31 and 2026-08-24. All 56 failed: 23 with :missing_linear_api_token and 33 with an empty query. So the feature has no use, and it wastes agent turns.

Also missed: Config.workflow_prompt/0 (config.ex ~L1070) falls back to @default_prompt_template, which begins "You are working on a Linear issue." A blank prompt_file on a GitHub tracker gets that text. Linear is tangled into core beyond the listed modules.

INVARIANTS: removing it breaks no safety or security invariant. LINEAR_API_KEY is only an optional secret in env/schema.ex, and no agent-env scrubbing depends on it.

Removing it does break these documented flows, which need doc edits in the same PR (AGENTS.md "Docs ship with the change"):
- `aiur init` offers linear as a tracker (init/questions.ex @tracker_kinds, plus the walkthrough in init.ex that already warns "Linear support is LIMITED and lightly tested").
- README.md, src/README.md (quick start and the linear-codex example), the aiur-intro skill ("GitHub or Linear"), docs-app index.md, reference/configuration.md L79/L112-115/L832, and skills.md (the .codex/skills/linear row).
- `make e2e` → test/aiur/live_e2e_test.exs (802 lines). It is Linear-only, not in CI, and cannot have run here, because no LINEAR_* variable exists in any .env.

LOC/ATTRIBUTION is wrong. The 894 lib lines leave out:
- codex/dynamic_tool/linear_graphql.ex (122 lines) and the Linear payload clauses in dynamic_tool/errors.ex
- the Linear branches in init.ex, init/questions.ex, init/resume.ex and init/templates.ex
- the LINEAR_* entries in env/schema.ex and env.ex
- in config.ex: the kind validation, the legacy linear: merge in prepare_tracker_config, the has_section?("linear") inference, @implicit_env_vars and the Linear default prompt
- the `_ -> Aiur.Linear.Tracker` fallback in tracker.ex
- the Linear error clauses in orchestrator/workspace_cleanup.ex and tracker_health.ex
- the Linear branch in workspace/layout.ex

The test cost is much larger than the ~323 lines claimed. The default fixture in test/support/test_support.exs (workflow_content) is tracker_kind: "linear". There are 596 write_workflow_file! calls in 108 files, and only ~241 set tracker_kind explicitly (169 github, 65 memory, 7 linear), so roughly 350 calls run on the Linear default. Five orchestrator and extension test files (dispatcher, orchestrator_status, orchestrator_deactivate, extensions, dynamic_tool) inject a fake Linear client through :linear_client_module. Removal therefore means moving the default fixture to memory or github first.

WHY CUT, NOT EXTERNALIZE: Aiur.Tracker.adapter/0 is a hardcoded case statement. There is no plugin or extension loader in lib and no upstream remote to stay in sync with. "Externalize" would mean building a new plugin-registry abstraction for an adapter with zero users, which defeats the stated goal of shedding abstractions.

The rationale is also overstated. The memory tracker stays either way, so the adapter boundary stays too. What removal actually deletes is the Linear-only parts: the TrackerConfig behaviour (only GitHub.Config and Linear.Config implement it, so it could collapse), the legacy linear: merge, the LINEAR_* env fallbacks and memo keys, the section-inference branch, and the Linear default prompt.

Suggested order:
1. Drop linear_graphql from @handlers (it is harmful now).
2. Move the test default fixture to memory.
3. Delete src/lib/aiur/linear, the Linear schema entry and env fallbacks, the init option, the e2e test and the docs rows in one PR.

challenge.note:
I could not refute the cut, so it holds. The LOC figure is wrong, though. It understates the code by about 3x, which makes the case for the cut stronger.

(1) Usage: none found in any source I checked.
- Configs: 16 config files contain the key: <private repo> (private), <private repo> (private), ~/.aiur/config, config.archon and 12 ~/.aiur/config.bak*. Every one has it only as the commented template line `# worker: { ssh_hosts: [], max_concurrent_agents_per_host: 4 }`. Zero set it uncommented. The other repo configs (aiur, aiur-research, the aiur-2675/2676/2677 and executor-runtime repos, kevinweaver-dev, archon, <temporary-checkout>) do not have the key at all. The live .aiur/examples/config.example line 201 is also commented.
- Runtime evidence: I checked all 34 real run logs under ~/.aiur/logs (2026-09-15 to 2026-09-26). All 328,781 telemetry `worker_hosts` samples are `[]`. The only non-null `worker_host` values are in test fixtures or test tmp output.
- AIUR_SSH_CONFIG is not set in ~/.aiur/.env or in any repo .env.
- Transcripts in ~/.claude/projects (58 files) show ssh_hosts values only as test fixtures (worker-a, worker-1, worker-01:2200) or as research and review discussion.
- No skill references the feature.

(2) Invariants: no safety or security invariant breaks. Cutting removes an attack surface: the SSH env neutralization (BASH_ENV/ENV/HOME/ZDOTDIR AcceptEnv) and the remote install of the #2356 agent token. Every non-nil worker_host comes from worker.ssh_hosts through Slots, the Dispatcher and AgentRunner.selected_worker_host, and resumes inherit that value, so the local nil path does not change. The cut needs these companion edits:
- Docs: configuration.md §worker, the src/README.md limitation notes (lines 639 and 653), and the scoping notes in apis/github.md:539 and guide/gui.md:119.
- The AIUR_SSH_CONFIG env var, in env/schema.ex:208 and .env.example:77. The check-env-example CI gate checks that pair. The schema describes the var as "used for git operations", which is wrong: only ssh.ex reads it.
- The live_e2e test "…with an ssh worker" (it uses a Docker SSH harness and is skip-tagged) and ssh_test.exs.

(3) LOC and module attribution: wrong, understated. The feature is not 199 lines plus about 150. The listed modules miss:
- workspace/remote.ex (47 lines, SSH-only)
- remote clauses in provisioner (~178), agent_skills.remote_install_script and its helpers (~128), workspace/remove (~69), git_metadata (~57), codex/app_server_port SSH.start_port (~55), agent_github_guard.remote_install_script (~51), hooks (~49), agent_command_installer (~47), bootstrap_image, layout, agent_scratch and CodexSandboxPolicy.remote_workspace_writable_roots
- the per-backend `remote_worker` capability flag (CodingAgent.remote_worker?, and `remote_worker: false` in open_ai_compat/registry.ex)
- the per-host slot logic
- worker_host passed as a parameter through about 40 lib files (821 occurrences)
- the analytics reduce.py and render.py `worker_host` handling

challenge.note:
Part of the claim holds: no real config sets an override key. The recommendation as written does not, for three reasons.

(1) THE BALANCE-BASELINE TRACKER HAS A USER. Its default path (take the first balance it sees as the baseline) needs no config. ProviderMeterProbe.balance_used_percent(:deepseek, ...) calls it on every DeepSeek meter probe (provider_meter_probe.ex:175). Live ledgers exist in 9 run state dirs under ~/.config/aiur/*/<repo>/balance-baselines/balance-baseline.json: aiur (2 dirs), archon, kevinweaver-dev, architecture-docs (2), khala (2), and one private repo not inspected. All hold a deepseek baseline, recorded between 2026-08-02 and 2026-09-17. Two aiur ledgers (2026-08-15 and 2026-08-22) have `reseeded_at` and `previous_amount`, so the top-up reseed path also ran in production. DeepSeek is enabled in ~/.aiur/config, its backups, config.archon, and the aiur-research family (priority: [codex, deepseek, claude]). 6 workspace agent.ndjson logs mention deepseek. So "0 mentions in retained telemetry" does not mean the feature is unused. If BalanceBaseline is cut, the dashboard meter drops DeepSeek's used% and shows dollars only. Only the `balance_baseline` config-deposit branch (configured_deposit plus the stale-config warning, about 30 lines) is truly unused.

(2) THE LINE COUNTS AND MODULE ATTRIBUTION ARE WRONG. open_ai_compat/config.ex (136 lines) is the only OpenAI-compat runtime resolver. It builds the registry instance, validates, fetches the API key from the env, resolves the model, and holds the Req request function and header normalization. Only backend_config/fetch_backend_config/merge_runtime_config and part of the @known_keys atomize list (about 25 lines) are override surface. The quirk behaviors (transport.ex:24/72/218, coding_agent.ex:288, conversation.ex:31) run from registry defaults and must stay. Realistic removable code: about 25 lines in config.ex, about 30 in balance_baseline.ex, about 10 for the openrouter provider block in transport.ex, and about 10 for the model_discovery opt-out. That is about 75 lines, not 437. balance_baseline_test (261) mostly covers the first-observed and reseed paths, which are in use.

(3) THE backend_configs MAP IS SHARED PLUMBING. Config.backend_config_sections folds top-level `<backend>:` and `agent.<backend>:` sections into agent.backend_configs for every known backend. So the real `agent.deepseek.enabled: true` and the `agent.codex.command` / `agent.claude.command` entries arrive through this map. model_catalog.ex:206 and init/agent_cli.ex:205 read backend_config(b)["command"] for codex and claude. The `command` key listed under this feature is meaningless for kimi/deepseek/openrouter, which have no CLI. But a rewrite that drops the generic map or its `command` read breaks codex/claude discovery and init. The model_discovery opt-out also applies to codex and claude CLI discovery, per configuration.md, so it is not scoped to OpenAI-compat backends.

The claim holds for these points: no current or historical config sets base_url, api_key_env, transport, default_model, model, management_api_key_env, balance_baseline, quirks.*, model_discovery or openrouter.provider.*. I checked 7 current repo configs, ~/.aiur/config and 14 backups; the 2 private ones were counted only. Claude transcript hits are code, plan and spec text, not operator use. OpenRouter needs no `model` override because config validation requires a model in the route (agent_validation.ex, CodingAgent.model_required?). Docs reference/configuration.md documents all of these keys, with an openrouter.provider example and a model_discovery:false example. Cutting them needs a docs edit, and scripts/check-config-docs.py will flag anything left behind. No safety invariant depends on them. @known_keys is only an atom-exhaustion guard.

Recommended action: simplify. Keep the registry-driven resolver, `enabled`, the generic backend_configs map with its `command` read, and BalanceBaseline's first-observed and reseed ledger. Cut the unused per-backend overrides, the configured-deposit branch, and openrouter.provider passthrough. Cut the model_discovery opt-out optionally, and make that decision for codex/claude too. Remove the matching configuration.md rows and examples.
