challenge.note:
The recommendation is wrong on its main premise, and moving these keys to a plugin would break documented core behavior.

(1) A repo that is not Elixir sets these keys. <local-checkouts>/kevinweaver-dev/.aiur/config sets max_concurrent_builds: 3 and build_start_stagger_seconds: 5, both non-default. That repo is Next.js (package.json, next.config.ts, no mix.exs). The comment next to those lines says "Two fleets at 32 would thrash", so the operator uses these keys to limit load across fleets on one host. They do have an effect there. BuildGate.gate_dir/0 is one directory per host user (~/.aiur/build-gate; the override is only a test seam). DispatchPolicy.build_gate/1 (dispatch_policy.ex:233, called from dispatcher.ex:2135) holds new dispatch when active >= capacity or queued > 0. So when the Elixir fleet's Mix builds fill the shared gate, the Next.js daemon stops dispatching. A plugin that loads only for Elixir repos would silently remove that hold.

(2) The "2/7" count leaves out defaults. max_concurrent_builds defaults to 4 and mix_scheduler_cap defaults to 4 (agent.ex:152 and :239; default_mix_scheduler_cap at :454). No current config sets 0, so the gate is on for all 7 configs. Every agent environment gets BASH_ENV, the gate environment variables and ELIXIR_ERL_OPTIONS. The <private repo> (private) and <private repo> (private) configs contain the keys only as comments, copied from .aiur/examples/config.example.

(3) Documented flows and safety measures depend on these keys:
- configuration.md:212 says the dispatch gate defers new admissions when build slots are busy.
- configuration.md:366-369 documents the hold-timeout alert, the retain window and a three-key opt-out. That opt-out is linked to agent.min_free_memory_mb, which stays in core through BuildGate.enabled?/1.
- guide/gui.md ("Read fleet and build pressure") documents the Analytics pressure chart built on gate status. The run_telemetry sampler, dataset, summaries and dashboard files, analytics_live, and the OCC charts and presenter all read it.
- `aiur status` prints a BUILD GATE line (agent_control_cli.ex:2402-2431).
- The aiur-run skill (SKILL.md:225-227 and :787) tells the Executor to control effective concurrency with "AIMD/build gates".
- BuildGateHoldMonitor is in the supervision tree (aiur.ex:313).
- Config.maybe_add_build_gate_root adds the gate to the sandbox roots, and open_ai_compat/command_runner.ex bind-mounts the gate and lock directories.
- The saturation root-cause analysis (docs/measurements/2026-08-03-daemon-saturation-root-cause.md:118) lists mix_scheduler_cap (#883) as shipped hardening against daemon crashes.

(4) The size and module list are wrong. The feature is much more than 1020 lines of Elixir. At commit 3339b88, src/priv also has build_gate.bash (1912 lines), build_gate_holder.py (1025) and build_gate_command_wrapper.bash (292), about 3.2k more lines that the snapshot does not include. agent_build_guard.ex is also part of it. About 20 lib files reference the gate, including dispatch_policy, dispatcher, agent_environment, workspace/hooks, claude/repl/command and config.ex. Moving it out would need a plugin contract across dispatch, sandbox, environment injection, telemetry and the dashboard, which is much more than moving a config key.

Recommended action (simplify): keep max_concurrent_builds, build_start_stagger_seconds and mix_scheduler_cap as core host-admission keys. Consider a language-neutral name, because operators already treat them as general build limits. Turn build_gate_max_hold_seconds and build_gate_retain_seconds into internal constants, because 0 of 22 configs set them. If a rewrite wants a language seam, put only the Mix command matching behind an adapter. Keep the host-wide build-pressure dispatch signal in core.

challenge.note:
I could not refute this. The cut holds for the three knobs only. The BrokerTimeout monitor must stay: turn the knobs into module constants (300s window, threshold 5, 600s dwell).

(1) No real use found.
- An uncommented-line scan found 0 set values in every config I could reach: all accessible checkout configs, the local Aiur config and backups, and local review copies.
- Three configs carry the keys only as the commented lines copied from .aiur/examples/config.example:81-83. One of them is the <private repo> (private) config; I checked only whether its lines are commented and did not read its values.
- The keys do not appear in any skill, any quick start, website/docs-app/apis/github.md, or any other docs page. The only docs mention is the three rows in reference/configuration.md:237-239.
- Transcripts mention the keys only in three places: the #2466 review (session 31796d96, which asked for a test that a configured threshold is not silently ignored), agents reading the schema, and the config.example copy. No session ever set or tuned a key.
- Git history: all three fields came in with 8b4a0bd95 (#2466), and the defaults have never changed.
- Alert ledgers: 30 alerts.ndjson files under ~/.aiur/logs hold 3 real system.github.budget_broker_retry events (2 in 20260925T042508Z, 1 in 20260926T052025Z) and 0 budget_broker_degraded events. The defaults were never even approached.

(2) Nothing documented or safety-related breaks.
- The only callers are the private helpers window_ms/threshold/dwell_ms in src/lib/aiur/github/broker_timeout.ex:273-294.
- Unset config already falls back to the schema default, so constants give the same behavior.
- The "operator derives the threshold from a quiet-period baseline" flow is written down (moduledoc, schema comment, docs row) but no one has ever used it. It is a design preference, not a safety or security invariant.
- Two tests encode the knobs and would be deleted or rewritten, not a contract anyone relies on: "configured threshold, window, and dwell control alert behavior" in broker_timeout_test.exs:58 (its configure_rate_signal! helper exists only for that test) and the defaults/validation test in workspace_and_config_test.exs:2585-2615. If a test needs different values, the GenServer already takes opts (check_interval_ms, emit_fun), so that is the injection point.
- Cutting also means removing configuration.md rows 237-239 and config.example lines 81-83.

(3) The size and module attribution are wrong.
- The "~25 lib lines" figure covers only schema/agent.ex: 19 lines of field declarations with comments at 251-269, 3 cast entries, and 3 validate_number lines.
- The config.ex accessors at about lines 1003-1032 add about 30 more lines, and the fallback code in broker_timeout.ex (config_integer/schema_default) adds about 20. The real cuttable surface is about 75 lib lines.
- broker_timeout.ex (295 lines) must NOT count toward the cut. The monitor is the only detector for the #2457/#2464 budget-broker fault. local_hold.ex:107 and :122 call its record/0, and it is started under the supervisor at aiur.ex:348. Its topics are routed in .aiur/alerts:112-118, and it produced real retry events this week.

A possible alternative is to merge this with the sibling agent.capacity_starvation_alert_after_seconds into one shared alert-dwell setting. On this evidence, a plain cut to constants is simpler.

features.description: Opt-in rtk shell-output compression for agents, admitted only when the host rtk config excludes gh; drives an analytics panel.
features.usage_evidence: Real-config scan (22 distinct files: 7 current incl. 2 private + 15 historical; flatten.rb/usage_matrix.tsv, see coverage_notes): agent.rtk.enabled 0/22 and 0 examples. Added 2026-09-03 (#2521, 1 commit).

features.raw_rewrite_notes: Remove key, module and analytics panel.

challenge.note:
I could not refute it. "Cut" stands, and the case for it is stronger than the stated reason. Four corrections follow.

(1) USE: none found.
- I scanned all 13 current .aiur/config files under <local-home>/github/everdred plus ~/.aiur/config. None mention rtk.
- `git log -S rtk` over .aiur/config, .aiur/examples and src/examples returns nothing.
- No skill, memory file or quick start mentions agent.rtk.
- In transcripts, the key appears only in the session that built it (31796d96) and in this research run.
- rtk 0.47.0 is installed at ~/.local/bin/rtk, but no Claude hook is installed. `rtk hook check "gh pr view 1"` still rewrites gh, so turning the flag on today would only return {:refused, :gh_rewrite_not_excluded}.
- `rtk gain` has recorded 10 commands in total, which looks like dev probing.
- Caveat: Kevin asked for this explicitly. On 2026-09-02 he wrote "for rtk, lets include analytics in analytics page to see how much we saved using it". His 2026-09-03 /goal said "rtk install for aiur agents, and rtk savings surfaced on the analytics page". Tell him about the cut; do not drop it silently.

(2) NO INVARIANT BREAKS, because the flag gates nothing on the agent path.
- Aiur.Rtk has exactly one caller: AiurWeb.AnalyticsLive.rtk_panel/0 (analytics_live.ex:409).
- rtk.ex says itself that it "never puts rtk on an agent's PATH and never installs the hook". The implementing agent's report confirms it did not touch agent_environment.ex or any settings.json.
- So agent.rtk.enabled only switches a dashboard panel on. The "gh-guard admission gate" gates only whether the panel shows a number. If an operator runs `rtk init -g`, agents' gh calls are rewritten whatever the flag says.
- The configuration.md:218 entry is therefore wrong where it says "Opts agents into rtk output compression" and "Aiur refuses to admit rtk". The panel text "Set agent.rtk.enabled: true to let agents filter shell output" is wrong too. Per AGENTS.md, a wrong doc is worse than a missing one.
- The feature summary ("admitted only when the host rtk config excludes gh") describes protection that does not exist.

(3) LOC is undercounted.
- The 261 counted lines are rtk.ex (241) plus the Rtk schema in agent.ex (about 21).
- The panel adds about 95 lib lines: the analytics_live.ex template at about lines 308-341, the rtk_panel and rtk_absent functions at 396-454, and the assign at 365. styles.ex:67-73 adds 7 more. The real lib total is about 360 lines.
- Tests: rtk_test.exs (155 lines) and about 36 rtk lines in analytics_live_test.exs (the :analytics_rtk_opts env at about line 1020).

(4) The reason is overstated.
- The docs do not "measure zero saving on common commands". They give one zero (`git log --oneline -30`, 2033 -> 2033 bytes) and one 92% cut (`ls -la`, 12724 -> 1044 bytes).
- The local rtk history shows a 70% average over 10 commands.

A better reason: the key is a mislabeled toggle for a panel that has never shown data. What you cut: the schema embed, rtk.ex, the panel with its CSS, both test files, and the configuration.md row.

AIUR_SUPERVISOR_TOKEN is present but blank in all three dotenv files that name it (~/.aiur/.env, aiur/.env, kevinweaver-dev/.env; names-only scan), so the API is disabled on every host. meta/recurring-issues.md Rank 2 (~110 citations): agents 'asked ten times over hours ... the Executor was forbidden to answer'; #2262 'supervisor token empty'. test_loc = decision_api/authority tests (shared with the decisions surface).

challenge.note:
The cut holds for the config keys and the supervisor policy. It does not hold for the module as attributed: cutting all of decision_authority.ex would remove a live safety floor.

USAGE (refutation failed):
- Configs: 0 active uses. The only hits in <private repo> (private) and <private repo> (private) are one commented-out line each, checked by line number only. An archon session transcript shows the same commented `# decisions:` line. No `decisions:` block is active anywhere.
- Token: AIUR_SUPERVISOR_TOKEN is 0 bytes in ~/.aiur/.env, aiur/.env and kevinweaver-dev/.env. It is not in the current shell env or in the live beam.smp environ (checked by name and length only).
- Stored state: no persisted supervisor answers. The only `supervisor_basis` hits under ~/.aiur and the repo .aiur dirs are code and doc copies.
- Transcripts: about 20 files mention the keys and about 15 mention /decide or /revise. All are code reading, research workflows, or a memory note. That note (architecture-docs memory aiur-answer-human-required-command.md) records that /decide and executor-answer both refuse human_required, and that the operator works around this with a DecisionStore.answer RPC as an operator actor.
- Skills: the documented Executor flow is `executor-answer` (aiur-run SKILL.md:518, references/executor.md:167), not the supervisor API. Only docs-app/reference/configuration.md:656-661 and guide/gui.md:241-245 document the keys and the token.

BROKEN INVARIANT IF THE LISTED MODULE IS CUT WHOLE:
- DecisionAuthority has two parts: the supervisor `evaluate`/`normalize_policy` code and the direct-Executor floor.
- The floor is `executor_answerable?`, `executor_authority_answerable?`, `executor_reversibility_answerable?` and the attributes `@delegable_authorities` and `@executor_answerable_reversibilities`, about 20 lines. It runs on every host:
  - DecisionStore:1515: executor-answer validation refuses human_required and non-reversible decisions.
  - DecisionStore:1983: executor-moot/withdraw (#2711).
  - DecisionExpiry:53: classifies expired decisions the Executor cannot answer.
- Keep this floor, either in DecisionStore or as a small module.

LOC ATTRIBUTION IS WRONG BOTH WAYS:
- Too high: about 20 of the 141 lines in decision_authority.ex are the live floor above.
- Too low: decision_delegation.ex (318 lines) is not counted, but it exists only to apply this policy to supervisor answers. Other uncounted supervisor-only code: the supervisor branch of DecisionStore.validate_answer_policy_context (lines about 1476-1502), `Config.supervisor_decision_policy`, and the `supervisor_policy` projection in DecisionAPI.encode_decision.
- Also not counted: decision_api_controller.ex (193), supervisor_auth.ex (91) and supervisor_token.ex (34).

COUPLING:
- With the default policy (empty allowlist), every supervisor decide/revise already fails closed with `kind_not_allowed`.
- So cutting only the keys leaves dead mutation endpoints. Decide this cut together with the Decision API mutation half (decide/revise, DecisionDelegation, supervisor_basis).
- DecisionAnswer and DecisionHistory still call `DecisionDelegation.validate_basis`. Since no persisted supervisor answers exist, removing these calls needs no data migration.

RATIONALE CORRECTION:
- The Rank-2 residual is not "the Executor cannot answer". The Executor answers delegable, reversible decisions through executor-answer (#2275).
- What is left is human_required decisions, which this policy can never delegate because `evaluate_authority(:human_required)` is absolute, plus non-reversible decisions.
- So the policy never addressed that failure, which is another reason to cut it.

Docs to remove with the cut: the configuration.md `decisions` section, and, if the API goes too, the gui.md token paragraph, the AGENTS.md Auth AIUR_SUPERVISOR_TOKEN sentences and the env/schema.ex entry.

challenge.note:
The recommendation to cut the `events.*` config section holds, but the stated evidence is wrong in two places. Cut the three keys and keep the debounce behavior as a constant.

1) block_state_debounce_seconds is WIRED. src/lib/aiur/agent_runner/events_digest.ex:113 and :183-187 read `Config.settings!().events.block_state_debounce_seconds` directly. This bypasses the accessor, so an rg for accessor callers finds only tests (events_digest_test.exs:260 and :286). The debounce is live behavior: it coalesces blocked/unblocked oscillation in the agent-visible digest. A cut must keep it as a hardcoded 10s window. A naive schema removal still works at runtime, because the `_ -> 10` fallback catches it. But the digest tests call Config.events_block_state_debounce_seconds() and would stop compiling. Also, src/test/fixtures/test.yaml sets the window to 30, so the tests currently run at 30s, not 10s.

2) codeowners_refresh_seconds is ALSO dead, so two keys do nothing, not one. Aiur.GitHub.CodeOwners starts bare at src/lib/aiur.ex:421 with no opts. It uses `Keyword.get(opts, :refresh_seconds, @default_refresh_seconds)` with 3_600. Config.events_codeowners_refresh_seconds/0 has no callers. The moduledoc at code_owners.ex:38 falsely says the config key drives the refresh.

3) custom_events_per_turn_max is dead as claimed. The documented contract ("Caps custom events per turn", default 5) is not enforced anywhere. EmitEvent.enforce_per_turn_quota caps only `progress`, at a hardcoded 2. It returns :ok for `custom.*`. The `:custom_event_quota_exceeded` payload at errors.ex:367 is never produced. This is a documented bound that is already absent, so a cut breaks no invariant. The rewrite must either drop the doc claim and the orphan payload, or implement a hardcoded custom.* cap. It must not carry the false doc forward.

Usage check: the only hits in real configs are one commented template line, `# events: { ...defaults... }`, from .aiur/examples/config.example:202. That line was copied into ~/.aiur/config, its backups, and the <private repo> (private) and <private repo> (private) configs, commented out in every copy. There are no uncommented `events:` blocks. Transcript hits are only file dumps of that template and config.ex. No skill or quick start references these keys. So "0 examples" should read "1 commented template line, 0 set".

LOC: events.ex is 25 lines (verified) and the accessors are ~15. Also delete or adjust these: the embeds_one at schema.ex:61, the private reader in events_digest (~6 lines), 2 smoke tests in schema_test.exs:723-743, 4 lines in fixtures/test.yaml, 3 doc rows plus the heading in configuration.md:584-590 (the check-config-docs lint must stay in sync), the example template line, the code_owners moduledoc, and the orphan errors.ex payload (~8 lines).

challenge.note:
The recommendation does not hold as written. It treats `alerts_file` / `.aiur/alerts` as a topic-to-sound map. In fact it is also the message catalog for the core alert feed, so externalizing it would break a documented flow and orchestrator control flow.

Evidence (snapshot 3339b88):

1. **Messages come from the file.** In `src/lib/aiur/alerts.ex:145-154`, `emit_alert` takes `message = override_message || config_message(definition_for_topic(topic))`. When that is nil, it returns `{:error, :missing_message}` before `AgentEventLog.write`, `AlertLedger.append`, the central `alerts.ndjson` write and the AgentPubSub broadcast. Only the Exchange publish happens.

2. **Most callers rely on it.** 40 of the 58 direct `Alerts.emit_system(` call sites in `src/lib` pass only `reason:` and no `message:`. Examples:
   - `tokens_exhausted` and `usage_limit_exhausted` (`turn_alerts.ex`)
   - `prewarm_blocked` and the startup `agent.todo` alert (`dispatcher.ex`)
   - `capacity_starved`, `decision_store_unavailable` and the tracker `agent.paused` / `agent.unpaused` alerts (`issue_sync.ex`)
   - `route.*`, `ci.wait`, and more

   These reach the ledger and feed only when `.aiur/alerts` defines a matching pattern with a `message`.

3. **A test documents the dependency.** `src/test/aiur/orchestrator/dispatcher_test.exs:2947-2952` says that without the alerts file, `emit_system` "returns {:error, :missing_message} — and the alert latches that depend on a `:ok` return (e.g. `prewarm_blocked_alert_active`) never engage." `test_support.exs:487-500` copies the repo `.aiur/alerts` into every test config as "the canonical alert definitions".

4. **Live logs confirm it.** Recent central `alerts.ndjson` files have 62 `issue.label.added.agent.in-progress` and 64 `agent.paused` entries. Both come from message-less emitters, and their text comes from the file.

5. **It is scaffolded and documented.** `aiur init` always writes `.aiur/alerts`, even when the user declines sounds (`init.ex:194`, `Alerts.ensure_alerts` runs unconditionally). The quick-start (`guide/quick-start.md:45`) and `cli.md:41` document it. `concepts/operating-aiur.md:41` says the file "Maps event-topic patterns to messages and optional sounds." Transcripts show agents adding new alert topics to `alerts.linux/macos.example` as part of shipping an alert, because that is where the message lives.

6. **`enabled: false` does not remove the dependency.** It gates playback only. The three public configs that disable sounds still read the file for messages. Repos with no `.aiur/alerts` (archon, kevinweaver-dev, and no `~/.aiur/alerts`) already lose these message-less alerts silently. That is a latent bug, and it shows the coupling.

Usage and LOC notes:

- **Usage.** The claim understates the dogfood repo. `aiur/.aiur/config` has no `alerts:` section, so it runs with the defaults: enabled, mapping mode. But `~/alerts` does not exist on this host, so those clips resolve to missing files and play nothing. The alert ledgers still record a selected `sound` for many entries (about 4.5k freedesktop and about 560 `~/alerts` wav selections). Selection always runs; that does not mean a sound played.
- **LOC.** About 250 lines are truly sound code: OS/category tables at lines 15-62, `select_sound` through `player_candidates` at 529-725, and the `Config.Schema.Alerts` fields. The definitions loader, path resolution and legacy-yaml warning (lines 69-101 and 369-527, about 190 lines) are the core message catalog, not sound. The count also leaves out `workflow.ex` `resolve_alerts` (about 25 lines), `config.ex` `alerts_settings`, and the template embedding in `init/templates.ex`.

Recommended action (simplify):
1. Decouple the message from the sound. Make `emit_alert` fall back to `reason` or the topic when no definition matches, or move the messages into code at the emit sites. This also fixes the silent drop in repos that have no alerts file.
2. After that, only playback (`enabled`, `use_os_default_sounds`, `sound_dir`, the player and OS tables, about 250 lines) can safely move out to a notifier that subscribes to the alert feed or Exchange.
3. The `sound` field in ledger, `agent.ndjson` and AgentEvents records would disappear. No consumer was found outside `alerts.ex` and `agent_events.ex`.

challenge.note:
The cut recommendation holds. I could not refute it, but the LOC and module attribution is wrong.

(1) Usage. I found no real use.
- Real configs: I scanned 54 .aiur/config* files under <local-home>/github/everdred plus ~/.aiur/config. No file has an uncommented `debug:` line. Three files contain only the commented template line from .aiur/examples/config.example:195 (`# debug: false ... --debug still wins`), which `aiur init` copies in. That line is not a setting.
- Transcripts: in ~/.claude/projects, `debug: true` appears in only 2 subagent transcripts, and both hits are test code (the LogFile.apply_config_debug tests).
- Skills: no skill uses the key. aiur-debug refers to "when debug is enabled" in general terms only. AGENTS.md and the CLI docs direct operators to the `--debug` flag.
- Callers: no other feature reads the `debug` field. The only consumer is Aiur.LogFile.config_file_debug?/0.

(2) Invariants. Cutting it breaks nothing.
- The key is only a bridge. apply_config_debug/0 (src/lib/aiur/log_file.ex:92-111, called at src/lib/aiur.ex:38) runs `System.put_env("AIUR_DEBUG","1")` when the flag is absent. Everything downstream (log_file, pane_manager, screen_grab, attach_pane, agent_list/state) reads AIUR_DEBUG. The engine sets the same variable from `--debug` (aiur-engine.sh:732).
- `restart` passes its extra args through to `dispatch_run --bg`, so `aiurdev restart --debug` still works. The only loss is "sticky debug without re-passing the flag", and nobody uses that.
- Removing the field does not reject existing configs, because Ecto `cast` ignores keys not in its permitted list. A stray `debug: true` would then be silently ignored (debug stays off). A rewrite may want to warn on that key instead.
- The only doc to update is configuration.md:32. No documented flow depends on the key.

(3) LOC and attribution are wrong. The key is not "a field in schema.ex + reads (~10)".
- Schema: 2 lines (the field at schema.ex:45 and the cast entry at :149).
- Real body: about 30 lines, including the docstring, in src/lib/aiur/log_file.ex (apply_config_debug/0 and config_file_debug?/0), plus the call at src/lib/aiur.ex:38.
- Also removed: the docs row, the example line, the tests (the log_file_test.exs "apply_config_debug/0" describe block of about 95 lines, and workspace_and_config_test.exs:2690), and the comment at config.ex:171.
- Aiur.Config.settings_uncached/0 must NOT be counted as cuttable. telemetry_enabled?, upgrade_check_enabled?, Rtk.enabled? and aiur.ex (log_base_branch and others) share it.
- Origin: commit ec76c3b55 (#403) added 142 lines.

Recommendation: cut, with a corrected footprint of about 35 lib lines and about 100 test lines.

features.description: Aiur.Config.Paths: log root, repo name, sanitize, and per-repo durable state directories (decisions, usage ledger, executor, takeover, balance baseline...). Not operator config keys.
features.usage_evidence: codebase/feature-boundaries.md: Config.Paths has 20 boundary callers. No config key; used on every run.
features.raw_rationale: A runtime-state path registry living in the config namespace; it couples every stateful package to Config.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Move to a small runtime-state/paths package (merge with the state-store surface); each package registers its own path key.

challenge.note:
The recommendation does not hold as written. Its point about the namespace is fair, but the proposed merge has the wrong target, and its note that "each package registers its own path key" makes the design worse.

(1) The registry claim is overstated, and the attribution is partly wrong. The LOC counts are correct: src/lib/aiur/config/paths.ex has 354 lines and config_paths_test.exs has 229. But the module registers only 8 durable leaves:
- current-run-membership
- progress-retention
- usage-ledger
- usage-aggregate
- usage-compaction
- executor-takeover-alerts
- balance-baselines
- the decision/runtime root itself

About 12 other stores already choose their own leaf or file name under runtime_state_dir/decision_state_dir. Examples:
- workspace/ownership/store.ex uses "workspace-ownership"
- metrics.ex uses "metrics"
- executor_command_attention.ex uses "executor-command-attentions"
- dispatch_budget_store.ex uses dispatch-budgets.json
- branch_ref_store.ex uses branch_refs.json
- session_handle and subscription_store use their own state leaves
- global_pause, ci_approval, pr_ready, tool_call_ledger and resource_store name their own files

So per-package path keys are already the usual pattern. The feature lists an "executor" state dir, but Config.Paths has none. Executor.StatePaths resolves that dir through RepoBase.state_root (~/.aiur/repo/...), which is a second state root outside this module. The same research's feature-boundaries.md (~line 859) recommends the opposite direction: move RepoBase's state path INTO Config.Paths.

(2) The merge keeps the Config dependency it says it removes. Paths does not call Aiur.Config directly. It depends on Config through Tracker.project_identity, and Tracker.adapter calls Config.settings!().tracker.kind. Moving the module to a "runtime-state package" keeps that upward edge unless project identity is injected. With a LOC saving of 0, the merge is only a namespace move.

(3) "Merge with the state-store surface" puts the wrong things in a state package:
- sanitize/2 is the documented byte-identical join key for workspace dirs (Workspace.Layout), opencode ids (OpenCode.Config), hook-settings slugs and test-reset paths. Tests guard its historical transformation byte for byte.
- repo_name/project_name build the file prefixes that ~10 stores use.
- log_root_dir is per-launch and not durable state at all.
Workspace naming should not depend on a state-store package.

(4) These invariants must survive any change:
- The on-disk layout is $AIUR_BG_STATE_DIR (aiur-engine.sh default ~/.config/aiur; aiurdev --test sets a sandbox dir) / AIUR_INSTANCE_KEY / repo leaf / leaf. It holds live state on this host: ~12 instance-key dirs for aiur, archon, khala, architecture-docs, kevinweaver-dev and 2 private repos. Each has usage-ledger, usage-aggregate, usage-compaction, current-run-membership, progress-retention and other leaves. Renaming a leaf or changing how the root is built orphans that state.
- decision_state_dir fails closed when AIUR_INSTANCE_KEY or the project identity is missing.
- The resolved path must stay inside the root (PathSafety containment).
- Each subsystem gets a distinct leaf, so no subsystem can replay another's state (stated in the moduledoc).
Spreading the 8 leaves across packages removes the one place where anyone can review that the leaves are distinct. Nothing checks for collisions today.
- The 9 Application env override keys are test seams used by 31 test files.

(5) There is no external use. Docs, skills, the launcher and memory do not reference Config.Paths. It appears in 70 Claude transcripts, but only as code reading, with no RPC invocations, so there is no wire contract.

Suggested action: keep one central path registry. Move it out of the Config namespace into the kernel, and inject project identity. Move sanitize, repo_name and project_name into a kernel identity helper. Put the ~12 hand-rolled leaves and RepoBase.state_root into the registry instead of spreading its 8 leaves out. Keep every on-disk path byte-identical.

challenge.post_review_privacy_redaction: 2026-09-28: removed a private tracker value from the note; counts and verdict unchanged
challenge.note:
I tried to refute the cut and could not. I found no real use and no safety or security invariant that the cut would break. Some figures in the brief are slightly off, and the cut has doc and test costs the brief does not list.

(1) Usage (checked again):
- Configs: no live tracker.linear, top-level linear:, kind: linear or project_slug key in ~/.aiur/config, the ~/.aiur/config.* variants and backups, any <local-checkouts>/*/.aiur/config, or any workspace config. The two private configs and ~/.aiur/config match only on a public init-template comment line; private config values are withheld.
- Other hits are only test-harness fixtures under ~/.aiur/agent-tmp, created by the mix-test default tracker_kind "linear".
- Boot logs: 30 of 30 boots that log disabled_integrations say "Linear tracker off". No LINEAR_* key exists in ~/.aiur/.env or any repo .env.
- linear_graphql calls: there are 14 `tools.linear_graphql(` strings in 13 Codex sessions, but only 3 structured calls (workspaces khala/102, khala/139, architecture-docs/18). All 3 returned missing_linear_api_token. Khala's "KHA-146" is Khala's own ID scheme, not Linear.
- Linear skill reads: 9 sessions contain commands that read .codex/skills/linear/SKILL.md, not 3. Most are from a 2026-08-09 batch in GitHub-tracked aiur workspaces, so they are also misfires.
- GitHub: every issue or PR that mentions Linear was opened by its-everdred or its-applekid. There are no external reports.
- #1067 ("Bring Linear workflows to GitHub parity") was closed on 2026-08-08 with "fleet is GitHub-only… Refile if a Linear user appears".
- Public reach is small: the repo is public with 4 stars and 0 forks, and aiur-cli had 207 npm downloads in the last month.

(2) Documented flows and invariants:
- Nothing else in the system calls Aiur.Linear.*. The only callers are Tracker.adapter/0 (the `_ ->` fallback clause), the dynamic tool, and a docstring.
- The tool list really is sent unconditionally: DynamicTool.tool_specs() goes to Codex (frames.ex:52), Claude (claude/coding_agent.ex:234) and OpenAI-compat (tool_spec.ex:109). So every agent turn is offered a Linear tool that cannot work.
- The Linear adapter is already a partial stub: comments and PR functions return empty results, and add_label/remove_label return :unsupported. Label-driven behaviour such as agent:paused and rework therefore cannot work on Linear. The init wizard itself warns "Linear support is LIMITED and lightly tested".
- Cutting does not weaken any security invariant. It removes a raw GraphQL mutation surface that uses daemon-held credentials.
- Cutting does falsify public claims, and those must be edited in the same PR:
  - website/index.html:149, website/public/llms.txt, README.md:32 and packaging/npm/aiur-cli/README.md:32
  - .claude/skills/aiur-intro/SKILL.md:18,105
  - docs-app index.md:24, skills.md:60 and configuration.md:79,112-115,832
  - the src/README.md:94-95 Linear quick start and the linear-codex example pair (55+10 lines)
  - AGENTS.md:83,161
- Test cleanup the cut needs: test_support.exs:1149 defaults tracker_kind to "linear" and must move to memory. core_test.exs:312,387 assert that the linear-codex example parses.
- Also remove two leftovers: the Config default prompt "You are working on a Linear issue" (config.ex:25), which is also the fallback prompt for non-Linear configs, and the Linear wording in workspace.before_remove.

(3) Line counts and attribution:
- 599+63+197+122 = 981 lib lines is correct, and the skill is 388 lines at 3339b88.
- The brief does not count Schema.Linear (tracker.ex:183+), the init wizard and resume paths, env schema entries, workspace_cleanup and tracker_health clauses, errors.ex messages, linear_graphql_test.exs (113 lines), or the example pair.
- Outside the feature there are about 89 true Linear lines in lib and 339 test lines across 36 files. "~160 references" is roughly right, depending on how you count.
- 14 commits touched these paths since the 06-02 rename, not 11. The recent ones (#2425, #2172, #2023, #863, #803) are carrying cost that GitHub-driven changes forced onto the Linear adapter.

Advice for the rewrite: keep the Tracker behaviour and the memory adapter as the extension seam, and cut Linear, its dynamic tool and its skill completely.

challenge.note:
The usage claim holds, and cutting the REPL and Remote Control feature is still right. The recommendation fails as written because two of the listed modules also hold code that the whole fleet uses. Deleting them as listed would break process reaping, pause handling and rate-limit fallback for every backend. Move that code out first, then cut the rest.

USAGE (checked independently, confirms none-found):
- 54 .aiur/config files under github/everdred, plus ~/.aiur/config and about 20 ~/wt-* worktree configs: no uncommented `remote_control: true`, `+remote` or `claude-repl`. The only matches are commented `remote_control: false` template lines in <private repo> (private) and <private repo> (private) (content not quoted).
- ~/.aiur/logs: 81 of 81 "Resolved backend" lines say `remote_control=false`, and 0 name `backend=claude-repl`.
- The 9 "claude-hook" hits are strings in the khala repo's own source code (`claude-hook-steer`/`claude-hook-sync`), not calls to Aiur's endpoint.
- `gh issue list --label model:remote` finds only #370, closed 2026-06-25.
- No references in archon, khala or archon-docs.
- Executor transcripts mention it only while reading code. The aiur-monitor `AIUR_ALERT_NOTIFY_RC_COMMAND` belongs to the operator's own Claude surface, not this code.

WHAT BREAKS IF THE LISTED MODULES ARE DELETED:
1. remote_control.ex (726 lines): about 425 lines are the generic process kill/reap toolkit, used by every backend:
   - lines 218-487: `graceful_kill`, `graceful_kill_tree`, `process_tree`, `process_group_*`, and the identity-checked pidfd `reap_process*` functions
   - lines 530-684: `reap_workspace_agents`
   - callers outside this feature: Shutdown (`reap_workspace_agents`), AgentTeardown, ProcessReaper, PauseContainment, Workspace.Ownership.Guardian, Git, AgentResourceGuard, AppServer.Adapter, Codex.AppServerPort (`defdelegate process_group_for_pid`), and Claude.CodingAgent.
   - The guardian's identity-verified reap (no kill after PID reuse) is a safety rule. It lives in this file.
   - This code was still being extended in August (#2080, reap orphans).
2. remote_control_mode.ex (340 lines):
   - `teardown_for_redispatch/3` is the teardown RateLimitFallback uses for its codex<->claude reroute (line 431).
   - `add_issue_label` and `remove_issue_label` are used by RateLimitFallback and by PauseResume `clear_pause_override` (the agent:paused removal path).

ATTRIBUTION ERRORS:
- 3682 LOC overstates the feature by about 425 lines of shared code.
- The "RC checks in ~20 modules" claim mixes two things. pause_containment, process_reaper, shutdown and agent_teardown reference RemoteControl only for the kill helpers above, not for RC logic.
- The real RC-flag coupling is wider than the brief says: about 47 files outside the feature, including:
  - TUI: agent_list/input.ex `r` key, and rc_pane_borders.ex (53 lines, not attributed)
  - dashboard: OCC units_control_policy and agent_routing_preview
  - config: the `+remote` routing grammar in routing_value and agent_validation
  - init labels (`aiur init` creates model:remote)
  - coding_agent registry: `remote_transport`, `fallback_backend`, `rc_display_tail`
  - dispatcher: `repl_pane_id`
  - boot: lifecycle.ex `cleanup_stray_remote_control_servers`
  - interrupts.ex: `ReplAgent.interrupt`

DOCUMENTED FLOW:
- The feature is documented in docs index.md (backend table), concepts/operating-aiur.md "Remote control", ticket-lifecycle.md (model:remote, created by aiur init), configuration.md (`agent.remote_control`, `+remote`), cli.md, and AGENTS.md (`--no-dashboard` rejection).
- A cut must update those pages and stop init from creating the model:remote label. That work is required, but it does not block the cut.
- Cutting the feature also removes an authenticated POST /api/v1/:id/claude-hook write route and the edits to ~/.claude.json trust, which shrinks the attack surface.

RECOMMENDED SCOPE:
1. Extract the kill/reap toolkit into a neutral module (for example Aiur.ProcessTree).
2. Move `teardown_for_redispatch` and the label helpers next to their other callers.
3. Then cut repl_agent, repl/*, hook_events, hook_settings, transcript_tailer, display_tailer, the RC-only part of remote_control.ex (about 300 lines), RemoteControlMode's promote/demote code, rc_pane_borders, and the RC-flag branches listed above.

It is a viewer, not an agent backend.

No chat-pane recordings exist (find ~/.aiur/logs -name "*.ansi" = 0). Executors launch headless: --bg in 136 transcript commands (Claude 9, Codex 127). opencode.* keys set in 4 of 16 distinct configs; pre_warmed_sessions defaults to 3 (archon sets 0). opencode.db holds no Aiur-injected agent sessions now (sessions are GC'd, so history is unknown). 48 commits since June.
features.raw_rationale: One of the largest blocks in this surface (45 modules, 9k lines) couples Aiur to a third-party app's private SQLite schema and CLI, for a pane the operating mode (headless + dashboard/CLI) does not use.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Replace with a plain transcript tail (logs/agent.md) in the TUI chat pane, or move the whole TUI to its own package. Delete bridge, slots, attach pool, session writer, SQLite injection and theme. Coordinate with the TUI surface inventory.

challenge.note: The evidence does not support deleting the agent chat capability or booking an 8,500-line saving. Aiur's documented human-driven foreground mode opens a live chat pane; AGENTS.md makes real TUI chat interaction the manual acceptance path. The 2026-09-29 native Muse acceptance used that path to display a skill read, an allow-once approval, a scoped tool result and a delivered follow-up. The inherited usage sample counts mostly headless runs and has no retained pane recordings, but a missing recording is not evidence that foreground users do not use the pane. The existing bridge's private opencode SQLite dependency is a valid simplification target. A plain transcript-backed TUI can replace it only after feature parity for rendered tool/prose output, typed operator input, queued delivery, approval commands, pause/resume and restart is demonstrated in the real CLI/TUI. Count removed lines after the replacement exists and includes its tests; moving the TUI to another package is relocation, not deletion. This challenge was performed by the continuing researcher, not an independent reviewer.

features.name: GitHub read cache, ResourceStore and agent gh state cache
features.description: Restart-durable GitHub state keyed by resource identity (ResourceStore) with change events and a single fetch entry point, a transport-level read-through cache with per-resource TTL policy and metrics, write-through deposits from Aiur's own mutations, the agent-side gh answer cache and its bridge/metrics, cache history, and view-state demand/sweep.
features.usage_evidence: On every read path. ~/.aiur/github-budget/state-cache holds 3,875 agent-cache files; github_resources.json exists in 10 state dirs. resource_store.ex: 22 of 23 PRs touching it were fixes (96%). Open issues #2413 (three caches, none reads the others) and #2245 (pollers bypass ResourceStore); read-cache hit rate regressed 9.0% -> 0.0% once (#2372).
features.raw_rationale: Three overlapping caches (ResourceStore, ReadCache, agent gh cache) duplicate one concept; freshness is a per-caller flag, which caused the blocked_by regression chain (merged-fixes 2.6, 2.9).
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Merge into one store that owns freshness (versioned deposits invalidated by webhook/poll events) and serves both the daemon and agent gh wrappers through one read path.

challenge.note:
The diagnosis is partly right, but "merge the three caches into one" breaks documented contracts and safety invariants. The evidence behind it is also inflated.

(1) The LOC is right: the 14 listed files total exactly 6,214 lines. The attribution is wrong in both directions.
- Five of the listed modules are not caches. That is about 1,370 lines: view_state_sweep, view_state_demand, cache_history, agent_cache_metrics and read_cache/metrics.
  - ViewStateSweep backs the documented config key `polling.view_state_sweep_seconds`. It is in the configuration reference and is set in a sibling repo's .aiur/config. It is also the divergence watermark that lets webhook loss be detected.
  - CacheHistory and AgentCacheMetrics feed the documented /github-cache page. That page shows the "Agent gh exact-shape hit rate" and "Not measured".
  - A merge plan says nothing about any of these.
- The bundle leaves out the real body of the agent cache. That is the cache_* half of src/priv/github_quota_guard.sh (3,403 lines at the snapshot; cache functions start at L1047).
- It also leaves out other GitHub cache layers: cache_inspector/* (about 840 lines), github_cache_live.ex (1,809), PollSnapshots, BoundedBlockedBy and CycleFetchCache (used from 5 lib files). So the "three caches" framing undercounts.

(2) A merge breaks documented flows and invariants.
- Agent cache: website/docs-app/apis/github.md "Shared agent reads" documents a byte-exact replay of `gh` stdout, keyed by output shape. agent_cache.ex explains why a stored REST body cannot stand in for it: gh field projection, Go JSON escaping and gojq. A reconstruction would silently corrupt what agents read.
  - The agent store is files read by a POSIX shell script, so it cannot be an ETS table. The two are already joined by identity through AgentCacheBridge, which carries invalidation only.
  - It has operator-facing env vars: AIUR_GITHUB_STATE_CACHE_ENABLED, _BYPASS, _TTL_MS and _WAIT_MS.
  - The docs name "a deliberate divergence from the daemon's ReadCache policy ... the two stores serve different callers with different invalidation reach".
- ReadCache: it exists because GraphQL returns no ETag. It is keyed by query {method, url, body}. ResourceStore is keyed by resource identity with REST validators.
  - The docs rule "A validator belongs to the thing it describes ... Writing a query's validator into a resource's key means any other writer of that key destroys or corrupts it" forbids folding one keyspace into the other.
- ResourceStore also holds per-version processed marks. These drive comment dedup and the self-echo suppression in "Comments arriving twice" and "Changes Aiur makes itself". That is a correctness invariant, not caching.
- Issue #2413 itself accepts "two stores with a documented sync" as a valid outcome, and that sync partly exists already: AgentCacheBridge, plus #2347 bridging webhook invalidation into ReadCache.

(3) The usage evidence is real but the numbers are inflated.
- Live checkpoints are active: khala github_resources.json is 6.8 MB, written 2026-09-26; aiur's is 609 KB. The state-cache holds 3,726 files, 929 written since 09-24.
- The Executor has a memory recipe that RPCs ResourceStore.drop_data/drop_etag. That is an operator workflow tied to this API.
- "22 of 23 PRs were fixes (96%)" does not reproduce. On main, 12 first-parent commits touch resource_store.ex, and about half are features: #2113 integration, #2300, #2331, #2332, #2336, #2150.

On the blocked_by chain (#2553, #2710, #2720), the root cause was an optional `revalidate:` flag with an `opts \\ []` default in Issues.hydrate_blocked_by, per ticket #2709. It was not the existence of three stores. ResourceFetch already makes freshness a required argument by design. The problem is that only 4 call sites use it (client.ex x2, human_review_gate.ex x2), and pollers bypass it (#2245).

The genuine duplication is narrow. ReadCache.Policy caches the REST `:issue`, `:pull` and `:comments` rows, which ResourceStore also holds as :issue, :pull_request and :issue_comments.

Recommend simplify, not merge:
- Route every resource-keyed REST read through ResourceFetch with required freshness, and delete the optional-flag APIs.
- Retire ReadCache's duplicated REST rows and keep it for GraphQL queries only.
- Keep the byte-exact agent cache and its identity bridge.
- Move view-state sweep/demand and the cache history/metrics into their own features.
- Keep the invariants: never cache verdicts, deny by default, strict reads, per-version marks.

features.name: GitHub credential pooling (tracker.github.credentials)
features.description: Registry and selector that spread daemon read traffic across several GitHub credentials (app_installation, machine_user, human) with per-credential write permission and enable flags.
features.usage_evidence: tracker.github.credentials (and every sub-key) is set in 0 of 68 config files (0 of 16 distinct, incl. private). Added 08-20..08-22 (5 commits), unchanged since.
features.raw_rationale: Unused multi-credential routing on the hottest code path.

challenge.note:
The usage claim for the pooling config holds. The "cut" recommendation does not, because the four modules also run the default single-credential path.

Usage checks:
- `tracker.github.credentials`, `token_env` or `writes:` is set in 0 of 210 `.aiur/config*` files, backups included, under <local-checkouts>/everdred, ~/.aiur and ~.
- Transcripts that mention `token_env` are development or research sessions (8989d0ab, the current session, 31796d96). None of them configures a pool.
- The GitHub issues that mention pooling (#2206, #2236, #2305 and others) are all closed.
- Correction to the brief: git history shows 8 commits, not 5. The latest change is #2515 on 09-02, not 08-22.

What a whole cut would break:
1. **Stable accounting identity (#2236, fixed by #2268, KTD3).** On every request, `transport.ex:118` calls `CredentialSelector.assign`. With one credential, `attach_accounting_identity` sets `credential_key = Credential.identity_key(legacy)`. `Budget` sends it to the broker as `--identity-key`, and `CredentialHeadroom.observe` stores headroom under that key. This keeps one continuous ledger while the App installation token rotates. The live broker `~/.aiur/github-budget/budget.sqlite3` holds 5 `credential_bindings` rows (5 identities). A cut would bring back the fragmentation bug that #2236 fixed.
2. **Agent budget identity.** `agent_environment.ex:472` builds a `%Credential{}` and calls `Credential.identity_key` to export `AIUR_GITHUB_BUDGET_IDENTITY_KEY` to the `gh` guard.
3. **Dashboard identity meters.** `BudgetMap.identity_meters` calls `CredentialSelector.headroom/1`, which reads `CredentialRegistry.configured/1` (which includes the legacy credential). `github_cache_live.ex:795` renders the result, and `guide/gui.md:161` documents it. `github-cost` also builds `CredentialUsage.rows` from `CredentialSelector.headroom/1`.
4. **CI readiness (#2515).** `ci_readiness.ex:477` uses `Credential.token_type/1` for the org-repository auth diagnostic.

LOC attribution: the 701 lines (121 + 202 + 299 + 79) are correct for the four files. They undercount the feature and overstate what can be deleted. The pool also reaches into:
- `tracker.ex` (`embeds_many` and `validate_unique_credential_ids`)
- `CredentialUsage.pool/1` and the pooled branches of `put_credential_view` in `github_usage_cli.ex` and `github_cost_cli.ex`
- `credential_pinned?` in `ci_readiness.ex:1096`
- 508 test lines (credential_registry_test and credential_selector_test)
- 7 rows in `configuration.md` and the "Credential pooling" section of `apis/github.md`

**Recommended action: simplify.**
- Delete the pool: the `GithubCredential` schema and the tracker embed, `configured_entries`/`from_schema`, the scoring in `choose`/`best`/`pick`, `intent`/`graphql_intent`, `eligible?`, `pooled?`/`by_id`/`by_token_key`, the `credential_pinned?` branch, and `CredentialUsage.pool` with its CLI branches.
- Keep one small single-credential identity module of about 60 to 80 lines: the legacy kind and identity, `identity_key`/`stable_identity`, `token_type`, and one headroom row for the meter.
- Resolve the legacy credential once, not on every request. Today each request makes two config reads plus two token resolutions, so the claim that this sits on the hottest code path is correct.
- Remove the doc rows and the pooling section in the same PR.

The rule that a human credential never writes becomes moot, not broken, because no human credential can enter the registry any more.

Fix history: github_comments_poller.ex 21 fix PRs (88% fix share); idle backoff chain #2025 -> #2818 open.

features.name: GitHub webhooks (ingress, delivery log, delivery modes, deposit/normalizer)
features.description: HMAC-verified /api/v1/github/webhook receiver, idempotent delivery log (72 h), per-repo delivery-mode state machine (polling vs proven webhook) with silence sweep and widened polling, and a deposit/normalizer that writes webhook bodies into the store and publishes the same events as the pollers.
features.usage_evidence: GitHub side (read-only gh api): only aiur-team/aiur has a hook (khala and archon, the September fleets, have none); all 3,524 deliveries GitHub still retains (2026-09-24..09-26) failed, last_response 502. Aiur side: the only non-empty webhook_deliveries.ndjson accepted 5,721 deliveries on 2026-08-12..08-15; every later state dir (aiur, khala, archon, architecture-docs, private) has 0. webhooks.repos set in 3 of 16 distinct configs; AIUR_GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET present in ~/.aiur/.env (name only). No webhook alert or wake topic appears in any retained log.
features.raw_rationale: Polling is the complete, default event source; the webhook path duplicates it (equivalence tests exist to keep the two identical) and has been failing unnoticed for the whole retained window.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Delete ingress, delivery log, delivery modes, deposit and normalizer. If quota later requires push delivery, add it behind the unified store as one more event source, measured per AGENTS.md "A claimed saving must be measured".

challenge.note: The frozen delivery census shows an actual failed webhook deployment, not an unused or redundant capability. `website/docs-app/apis/github.md` documents verified-delivery gating: failed or absent deliveries keep full polling and short cache TTLs; a proven delivery widens selected reconciliation reads and retires stale cache entries. Removing ingress would delete that conditional product contract and its event latency/reconciliation path. The cited 5,721 accepted deliveries in the earlier period show a real population, while 3,524 later 502 responses show the current path needs operational diagnosis. No quota saving may be claimed during the failed period, and the proposed 5,120-line deletion is a gross estimate that omits replacement work. Keep the capability while deciding whether to repair the deployment or replace transport; test loss recovery, signature validation and measured read displacement before any cut. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.
