features.name: CODEOWNERS author allowlist
features.description: Parses CODEOWNERS to decide whose comments are trusted directions to agents, refreshes it on a cadence, and edits CODEOWNERS from `aiur init`.
features.usage_evidence: Consulted by the event sanitizer for every comment event. .github/CODEOWNERS exists in aiur-team/aiur and aiur-team/khala, not in archon (gh api read-only). events.codeowners_refresh_seconds set in 0 configs. Four overlapping allowlists exist: CODEOWNERS, tracker.github.trusted_accounts (6 of 16 distinct configs), allowed_users (6), human_mergers (11, 1 private).
features.raw_rationale: Four trust lists answer the same question (who may direct or merge); CODEOWNERS parsing plus editing is 1.3k lines for it.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Merge into one trust policy: trusted_accounts (direct agents) and human_mergers (merge), optionally seeded from CODEOWNERS at init; drop the runtime parser/refresh and the init editor.

challenge.note: CODEOWNERS author matching is applied to comment content before agents see it; tracker trusted_accounts, allowed_users and human_mergers govern different identity/action questions. A single flat list would authorize people for actions they did not have before, or fail closed on legitimate repository owners. The frozen Codeowners module also handles path-specific rules and an explicit trusted-account fallback when no rule matches. Consolidate policy vocabulary and configuration ownership, but retain separate permissions for comment instructions, issue writes and merge authority; prove each against adversarial comments and missing CODEOWNERS. Dropping the runtime parser/refresh needs an equivalent current owner signal, not only an init-time seed. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

features.name: PR health scan and rework re-queue
features.description: Periodic scan of open PRs raising unmergeable-author, stale-unreviewed and rework-merge-only alerts, and moving a reworked PR back to human-review when its own diff changed since CHANGES_REQUESTED.
features.usage_evidence: pr_health.enabled true in 2 of 16 distinct configs (aiur and aiur-research). Retained alerts: system.pr_health.stale_unreviewed 82, unmergeable_author 54, rework_requeue_failed 0.
features.raw_rationale: The alerts are cheap and useful; the re-queue is one of five writers that decide rework state (merged-fixes 2.2).
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Move the re-queue rule into the single ticket-state authority (feature 02 notes); keep the scan as three alert checks.

challenge.note: The PR-health scan is configured in two of sixteen distinct configs and emits counted stale/unmergeable alerts, so retaining the scan is supported. ReworkRequeue writes a ticket state based on own-contribution diff since the latest CHANGES_REQUESTED review, distinguishing merge-only from addressed changes; that decision belongs in the single lifecycle authority if extraction preserves review-thread clearance, failed-write attention, head-change throttling and a bounded GitHub read policy. Do not merge it into a timestamp/head-SHA heuristic or erase the different alert classes. Actual net LOC saving and read rate require measurement after the move. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

features.name: PR watch and /aiur PR comment commands
features.description: Opt-in watching of human PRs via a watch label, repo-wide scan for one-off /aiur or @bot PR comment commands, and PR-anchored routing/teardown of agents working on human PRs.
features.usage_evidence: pr_watch.* is set in 0 of 68 configs (default enabled: false), so command_scan, pr_anchored and target selection branches never run. Executor transcripts show 24 lines mentioning /aiur watch|merge|rework or agent:watch, none enabling it.
features.raw_rationale: Default-off feature with no config enabling it anywhere.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Delete command_scan, pr_anchored, pr_command_scanner, the pr_watch schema and the gated branch in comment_polling/target_selection (~80 lines).

challenge.note: The frozen PrWatch schema defaults disabled, and the retained config census has zero of 68 enabling `pr_watch.*`; the one-off command and anchored human-PR paths therefore have no configured production population in that census. A cut is justified if a final census of shipped and external configs still finds no enabled deployment and there is no documented compatibility commitment. Remove the schema, poller, target-selection branch, docs and tests together, retaining safety that ignores human PR comments unless explicitly trusted. Count actual deleted lines, not the estimated branch size. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

features.name: Agent event bus (topics, subscriptions, publisher, sanitizer)
features.description: AMQP-style topic exchange for cross-ticket events, per-issue persistent subscription stores, universal agent subscriptions, restart-safe event ids, shared publisher, six-layer sanitizer and external-content wrapping for GitHub text, publication audit log.
features.usage_evidence: Carries every wake (9,760 wake records) and every agent-visible GitHub event; 126 per-ticket subscriptions.json files in retained logs; agents emitted 8,487 custom events (emit_event). Explicit subscribe calls: 3.
features.raw_rationale: The core event pipe between GitHub, agents and the Executor.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Simplify topic patterns to the few classes in use (ticket.<id>.{pr,ci,branch,agent,comment}, system.*) if the rewrite drops custom subscriptions.

features.name: Executor wake inbox and executor-wait (claims, roster, principal)
features.description: Durable identifier-only wake ledger per repo (<repo>.executor.wakes.ndjson + cursor + pending), bounded to 10,000 records; executor-wait long-poll with auto-claim; a leased single-owner claim with TTL, roster states (active/idle/stalled/expired) and principal registration for --executor runs; recovery commands.
features.usage_evidence: Wake records: aiur 4,749, architecture-docs 1,881, archon 810, khala 2,203, <private repo> (private) (private) 117 (census). Executor commands (Claude transcripts since 09-01 + Codex Executor sessions): executor-wait 31 + 795, executor-roster 10 + 26, executor-revoke 0 + 7, executor-release 1 + 0, executor-fast-forward 1 + 0, executor-claim 0 + 0, --executor 0 + 1. Executors also read the file directly (commands naming *.executor.wakes.ndjson, mostly tail -F: 254 + 72) and the khala Executor wrote its own wake-relay.py and native-wake-relay.py in its state dir.
features.raw_rationale: The inbox and wait are the Executor's main input and are used; the multi-consumer lease/roster/revoke/fast-forward machinery is barely used, and Executors still build relays around it.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Keep the ledger + cursor + a blocking wait that also pushes (one stream the Executor can follow natively). Replace claims/roster/principal with a single-owner lock and a staleness check.

features.name: Executor event journal, listener and custom executor.* events (listen/emit/subscribe)
features.description: Supervised daemon listener that reduces allowlisted events to wakes, a durable Executor event journal with cursor, and CLI commands to stream events, publish custom executor.* events and manage persistent Executor bindings.
features.usage_evidence: The journal is used only for decisions: 266 records across aiur/architecture-docs/archon/khala, of which 265 are executor.decision.requested/deferred and 1 is a custom executor.khala.monitor_check. Commands: executor-listen 0 + 11, executor-emit 0 + 4, executor-subscribe/unsubscribe/subscriptions 0 + 0 (Claude + Codex Executor transcripts).
features.raw_rationale: The listener that feeds the wake inbox is needed; the Executor-facing pub/sub surface is not used.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Keep the listener as an internal wake producer. Cut executor-listen, executor-emit, executor-subscribe/unsubscribe/subscriptions and custom executor.* topics (CLI handlers counted with the CLI surface).

features.name: Decision/Command store, delivery and Executor answer CLI
features.description: Durable event-sourced Decisions ("Commands") raised by agents: validation, provenance, attention classification, blocking gate, expiry, answer recording, delivery to whichever worker runs the ticket, dispatch tasks, dismissal/moot/escalation, history and query/projection; `aiur commands`, `aiur executor-answer|escalate|moot`.
features.usage_evidence: decisions.ndjson across 14 state dirs (~/.config/aiur/*/*): 595 requested, 81 answer_recorded, 285 decision_expired, 514 failed (delivery), 38 decision_mooted, 22 executor_escalated, 52 delivered, 45 consumed. Only ~14% of requests got an answer. Commands used: `aiur commands` 130 + 66, executor-answer 39 + 12, executor-escalate 23 + 12, executor-moot 9 + 2 (Claude + Codex Executor transcripts). Wakes: 143 ticket.agent.attention.operator-decision. Fix history area M: 17 fix PRs; decision_store.ex is the largest file in my surface (4,826 lines).
features.raw_rationale: Agents do need a way to ask and be answered, but 13k lines deliver an answer in 14% of cases and fail delivery more often than they succeed.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: A small ask/answer record keyed to the ticket: {question, options, blocking, answer, delivered_at}, answered by CLI or dashboard, delivered at the next turn via the agent queue. Drop attention classification variants, dispatch tasks, retained-index snapshots and legacy pagination.

features.name: Decision revisions, enrichment and decision latency metrics
features.description: Revision requests and their dispatch, supervisor enrichment of a decision, and a decision-latency metrics writer/collector (metrics/decision_latency.ndjson) feeding a dashboard latency panel.
features.usage_evidence: Across ~1,800 decision events in 14 state dirs there is no revision or enrichment event type (event types seen: requested, failed, decision_expired, answer_recorded, dispatch_queued, delivered, consumed, acknowledged, resolved, deferred, escalated, mooted, dismissed, dispatch_outcome_unknown, handed_off), and all 595 requested decisions carry revision_sequence 0 (rg revision_sequence), so no revision or `executor-answer --supersede` replacement was ever accepted. The metrics writer does run (decision_latency.ndjson: khala 607, aiur 706+85, kevinweaver-dev 382 lines) but its only reader is a dashboard panel.
features.raw_rationale: Unexercised workflow branches plus a metrics pipeline for a panel.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Delete revisions (this also removes `executor-answer --supersede`, which is the revision path), enrichment and decision_metrics; compute answer latency on read from the decision record if a panel needs it.

challenge.note: No revision/enrichment event appeared in the retained decision population, but `executor-answer --supersede` and `executor-moot` are documented emergency controls for withdrawing or replacing an answer before an agent receives it. A zero-use normal window cannot establish those recovery semantics are obsolete. The decision-latency writer does have retained rows and the dashboard reads them, so it is not a dead pipeline. Simplify the storage/metrics implementation if a read-derived latency preserves event-time, source freshness and unknown paths; remove revision only after proving an equivalent pre-delivery withdrawal/replacement contract. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

features.name: Supervisor Decision HTTP API (bearer token)
features.description: Machine-facing /api/v1/decisions read/decide endpoints for a supervising Executor authenticated by AIUR_SUPERVISOR_TOKEN, with fail-closed delegation/authority policy (decisions.supervisor_allowed_kinds).
features.usage_evidence: All 30 retained boots that log disabled_integrations report "Supervisor Decision API off (no AIUR_SUPERVISOR_TOKEN)". decisions.supervisor_allowed_kinds / supervisor_allow_non_reversible are set in 0 of 68 configs. Executors answered through the CLI (executor-answer) instead; 6 /api/v1/decisions mentions in aiur Executor transcripts and 1 decide call in architecture-docs.
features.raw_rationale: A parallel answer path that is never enabled; the CLI covers it.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Delete DecisionApi, its controller, supervisor auth/token, delegation/authority policy and the decisions config section. A future remote Executor can use the same RPC as the CLI.

challenge.note: The HTTP Decision API was disabled in 30 retained boots, with no configured supervisor_allowed_kinds in the sampled configs, which establishes zero current enabled population there. The proposal that a future remote Executor can use the same RPC as the local CLI is not an equivalent authenticated network contract: DecisionApi includes bearer validation, fail-closed delegation and authority checks. A cut may be attractive, but first decide whether the first-class agent-operated Executor mode needs remote decision submission, count external deployments, and either keep this authority seam or specify and test a replacement. Do not count moving its policy into a new adapter as deletion. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

features.name: Alert feed and ledger (aiur alerts, needs-attention)
features.description: Project-scoped durable alert ledger, structured alert emission (with optional sounds), alert topics and the feed read by `aiur alerts` and the watch actionable section.
features.usage_evidence: `aiur alerts` 143 + 459 invocations (Claude + Codex Executor transcripts). 37% of aiur wakes are needs_attention (census). alerts.enabled set in 11 of 16 distinct configs (sound switch). Fix history area J: 44 fix PRs; false/re-raised alert chain 2.15 still open (#2811, #2819).
features.raw_rationale: The Executor's primary attention signal. Its problem is lifecycle (conditions not keyed), not size.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Key each alert to a condition with an owner and a resolve rule; move sounds (alerts.use_os_default_sounds, sound_dir, alerts_file) to the TUI/Stream Deck package. Overlaps the observability surface inventory.

features.name: Asks (aiur ask / aiur asks)
features.description: Append-only Executor-authored requests to the human operator, listed by `aiur asks` and printed by status when blocking.
features.usage_evidence: meta/asks.ndjson: 5 records ever, all in aiur (0 in archon, khala, architecture-docs, private). Commands: ask 0 + 9, asks 3 + 5 (Claude + Codex Executor transcripts).
features.raw_rationale: Same shape as a blocking Command (question for a human); a second store for it is redundant.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Represent an ask as a Decision raised by the Executor principal; delete asks store and CLI.

challenge.note: The append-only Asks ledger records Executor-authored requests for a repository operator, with urgency, blocking and explicit done notes. Commands are agent-originated, ticket-addressed decisions with offered answers, versioning and delivery back to a worker. Representing an ask as an Executor-created Command changes who can answer, where the answer goes and how history is reduced; five records are too small a population to prove equivalence. A common notification/read model could reduce duplicate presentation, but a store merge needs schema, authority and migration proofs before deletion. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

features.name: Findings ledger (aiur findings)
features.description: Host-local NDJSON ledger of Executor findings with record/unfiled/slugs/digest views, used by /aiur-meta.
features.usage_evidence: meta/findings.ndjson: aiur 43, khala 13, kevinweaver-dev 9, archon 8 records. `aiur findings` 17 + 108 invocations.
features.raw_rationale: Small and used, but it is Executor tooling (aiur-meta), not daemon behaviour.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Move to the Executor skill package as a script over the same NDJSON file; no daemon RPC needed.

challenge.note: The host-local Findings ledger has an observed 73-record population across four public repositories and serves the aiur-meta workflow, which is a sensible external ownership seam. Preserve bounded NDJSON validation, append behavior, state-node discovery, latest-slug/unfiled reduction and digest diagnostics in a versioned skill-side tool, then migrate documented `aiur findings` callers. The existing daemon CLI wrapper can be deleted only after a usable replacement exists; moving the ledger to another package is relocation, not net LOC reduction. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

features.name: Executor takeover advisory alerts
features.description: Monitor that tracks each nonterminal ticket's convergence age and raises needs-attention takeover advisories at configurable thresholds.
features.usage_evidence: Retained alert logs: 46 system.executor_takeover.<n> and 6 .resolved. executor-takeover-alerts state dirs exist in 6 state dirs. executor_takeover_* keys set in 0 configs (defaults 8 h / 1 h).
features.raw_rationale: 1k lines (monitor, snapshot, store) for one age threshold.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Compute convergence age in the status projection and raise one alert from the alert lifecycle; drop the separate monitor and store.

features.name: Executor handoffs
features.description: Seeds the machine-local executor/handoff.md per repository; the aiur-handoff skill writes and reads timestamped handoff documents.
features.usage_evidence: 86 handoff files: khala 61 (58 on 2026-09-18, median gap 4.4 min), aiur 18, archon 5, architecture-docs 2 (census). aiur-handoff Skill invocations: 3 (Claude Executor transcripts).
features.raw_rationale: Tiny code; the value is in the skill. The khala burst is a skill/Executor behaviour problem, not a code one.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Keep in the Executor skill package; add a minimum interval or dedupe in the skill.

features.name: Executor-to-agent messages (aiur message)
features.description: Enqueues Executor text on an agent's native queue, delivers at a safe checkpoint or interrupts, auto-resumes paused entries, with message-id idempotency and delivered/queued/unknown outcomes.
features.usage_evidence: `aiur message` 53 + 275 invocations (Claude + Codex Executor transcripts). Fix chain: #1800 -> #2155 (enqueued reported as delivered).
features.raw_rationale: The Executor's direct channel to agents.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Keep; share one delivery path with decision answers (feature 35). Modules overlap the orchestrator surface.

features.name: Build Order graph, catalog and CLI (daemon side)
features.description: Planning layer over GitHub issues: build-order root labels and sub-issue/blocked_by graphs, event-sourced catalog store, selected-root projection with cadence/policy, pack status on disk, ad-hoc source, ticket detail and history providers, progress rendering, `aiur build-orders`.
modules: src/priv/build_orders/*.json + README (2,515 lines of seed packs, in git 3339b88)
features.usage_evidence: GitHub search (read-only): 7 aiur, 3 archon, 1 khala issues carry the build-order root label. Pack dirs: aiur 6, architecture-docs 4, archon 2, khala 1 (+ private). `aiur build-orders` 32 + 36 Executor invocations; /build-orders referenced 72 times in Executor Claude transcripts. tracker.github.planning_* set in 5 of 16 distinct configs; build_order.* keys in 0. 56 commits 07-13..09-18.
features.raw_rationale: Used a few times per repo, but it is a separate product (planning graph + views) that mostly reads GitHub; 11.5k lib + 8.6k web lines is the largest block in my surface.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Split into a Build Order package that reads the tracker store and publishes views; drop the event-sourced catalog cadences, ticket-history provider and selected-root policy layers (~4k deleted) in favour of on-demand graph reads.

challenge.note: Build Order is used in the counted pack and CLI populations, and `codebase/feature-boundaries.md` assigns it a coherent domain boundary but also records tracker, catalog, dashboard and projection dependencies. The raw proposal combines a plausible package seam with unproven deletion of catalog cadence, ticket history and selected-root policy. On-demand graph reads do not automatically preserve freshness, bounded GitHub cost, recursive membership or historical context; the inherited P0 detail-loop finding also makes read policy a correctness issue. Extract a package inside the repository after its identity, event, cache and read-model contracts are characterized. Defer repository separation and any 4,000-line deletion claim until equivalent behavior and measured physical lines exist. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

features.name: Build Order dashboard pages
features.description: LiveView /build-orders catalog and root pages: graph, grid model, breakdown, selected root, ticket context drawer, usage/analytics scopes, presenters and data/planning sources.
features.usage_evidence: No page-view log exists. /build-orders appears in 72 Executor transcript commands (curl/screenshot checks, mostly during development). The Build Order cadence docs say a headless run with no page open buys no catalog reads.
features.raw_rationale: Goes with the Build Order package (feature 44); overlaps the dashboard surface inventory.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Move with feature 44; collapse planning_source (926) / data_source / source_runtime / context_runtime layers into one view model (~2k deleted).

challenge.note: The dashboard pages are a consumer of the Build Order read model, not a free-standing extraction merely because they share a name. No page-view telemetry exists, so 72 transcript URL mentions cannot measure ordinary use. The proposed collapse of PlanningSource, DataSource, SourceRuntime and ContextRuntime needs behavior tests for demo/no-source, selected root, loading, stale/error and ticket detail/history states. Keep the Phoenix presentation in the web app while moving domain reads behind an explicit contract; count any deleted lines after the replacement, not from an estimated 2,000-line collapse. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

features.name: aiur-build planning skill (Build Order pack authoring and publication)
features.description: Executor skill that decomposes a feature into a validated planning pack and publishes it as GitHub issues with blocked_by edges; ships 14.5k lines of Python validators/publisher (3.4k of them tests) and 1k lines of markdown.
features.usage_evidence: Skill invocations: 2 in Claude Executor transcripts (archon, architecture-docs); SKILL.md read 20 + 9 times in Codex sessions. 13 pack dirs and 11 labelled roots exist (feature 44).
features.raw_rationale: A standalone planning/publishing tool larger than most daemon subsystems; it only needs GitHub, not the daemon.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Move to its own skill/plugin repo; test_loc here is the Python tests inside the skill (not src/test).

challenge.note: The planning-only `aiur-build` skill declares that it prepares durable packs and never runs Aiur or implements tickets; that is a real ownership seam from the daemon. The source inventory counts actual pack directories and skill reads, so the skill is not dead. Externalize only as a separately versioned skill/plugin with its planning contract, documentation links, template loading and tests intact; ensure a later `aiur-run` can consume the same pack schema. Moving the skill to another repository removes no product complexity and creates no net LOC saving by itself. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

features.name: Agent skill installer and bundled aiur agent skills (aiur-agent, aiur-debug, design-import)
features.description: Embeds skills at compile time and installs them into every ticket workspace under .claude/skills and .codex/skills (symlinks), plus the per-turn shared agent prompt that routes agents to aiur-agent.
features.usage_evidence: aiur-agent: 1,087 Skill invocations by Claude agents and ~8,500 SKILL.md reads in Codex sessions, 94% of which are agent sessions (exec/command lines only; the skill list injected into every session is excluded). aiur-debug: 0 Claude invocations, 35 Codex reads. design-import: 0 and 0.
features.raw_rationale: The agent operating manual is read on essentially every ticket turn.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Keep aiur-agent and aiur-debug; drop design-import (0 reads) from the workspace set. Skill-text tests (aiur_agent_skill_test 842 lines) could shrink to link/structure checks.

features.name: Vendored Compound Engineering skills (31 skills, pinned 3.19.0)
features.description: The complete pinned Compound Engineering skill set vendored into .claude/skills (with .codex symlinks) and installed into every ticket workspace, refreshed by scripts/update-compound-engineering-skills.
features.usage_evidence: Reads in Codex sessions (exec/command lines; 94% agent sessions) + Claude agent Skill invocations: ce-code-review 3,363 + 103, ce-work 1,091 + 4, ce-plan 895, ce-doc-review 393, ce-simplify-code 355, ce-debug 349, ce-commit-push-pr 313, ce-resolve-pr-feedback 225 + 2, ce-commit 141 + 1, ce-brainstorm 85. Twenty skills have 0-3 agent reads: ce-babysit-pr, ce-compound, ce-compound-refresh, ce-dogfood, ce-explain, ce-handoff, ce-ideate, ce-optimize, ce-polish, ce-pov, ce-product-pulse, ce-promote, ce-proof, ce-riffrec-feedback-analysis, ce-setup, ce-strategy, ce-sweep, ce-test-browser, ce-test-xcode, lfg (25,506 lines).
features.raw_rationale: Ten skills carry the agent workflow; the other twenty are vendored bulk that no agent reads.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Ship only the used subset into workspaces, or install the upstream plugin at a pinned version instead of vendoring; the Executor can still load the full plugin in its own session.

features.name: Codex-native git skills (commit, push, pull, land, linear)
features.description: Codex-only skills under .codex/skills for commit, push/PR, merge-based pull, land (with a 621-line land_watch.py) and raw Linear GraphQL.
features.usage_evidence: Codex exec reads: commit 119, push 89, pull 46, land 35, linear 3. skills.md also lists a `debug` Codex skill that does not exist at 3339b88.
features.raw_rationale: Duplicates ce-commit / ce-commit-push-pr, which agents read more (141 and 313).
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Merge commit/push into the CE commit skills; keep pull/land only if the merge policy needs them; delete linear (feature 03) and fix the stale debug entry in skills.md.

challenge.recommendation: merge only overlapping commit and push wording after command-by-command parity
challenge.note: The raw census records commit 119, push 89, pull 46, land 35 reads, so these skills are exercised. .codex/skills/land/SKILL.md and land_watch.py carry a long-running merge workflow distinct from ce-commit; pull has merge policy and linear has a raw GraphQL role. Removing them wholesale would drop behavior. Deduplicate shared prose only after mapping command, guard and lifecycle parity; the 700 LOC estimate is unverified.

features.name: Executor skills (aiur-run, aiur-monitor, aiur-meta, aiur-intro, release)
features.description: Skills loaded by the Executor session: run operation end to end, monitoring, hourly meta audit, first contact/install, release. (aiur-build, aiur-handoff and aiur-debug are listed separately.)
features.usage_evidence: Claude Executor Skill invocations since 09-01: aiur-run 7, aiur-meta 1. SKILL.md reads across all Codex sessions (exec + older command format): aiur-run 161 + 129, aiur-monitor 40 + 10, aiur-meta 16, aiur-intro 8 + 6, release 0. /aiur-meta durable logs stopped after 2026-09-11 (census).
features.raw_rationale: Executor procedure, not daemon code; they version with the operator, and tests in src/test assert their text.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Move to an Executor skill package with its own lint; cut aiur-run by ~1.5k lines of incident-specific rules (the file is 4.2k lines).

challenge.recommendation: keep versioned Executor contracts with the repo and modularize aiur-run
challenge.note: The Executor skills govern operations against the corresponding daemon and are documented at website/docs-app/skills.md. The large aiur-run file may contain reducible incident prose, but externalizing 6,562 LOC moves it and can separate instructions from the version they operate. No line-level demonstration shows 1,500 incident rules obsolete. Split stable contract, runbook examples and historical notes while retaining repo-versioned distribution.

features.name: ElevenLabs provider (speech-to-text, TTS, quota meter)
features.description: Realtime STT sessions over Mint.WebSocket for Stream Deck/dashboard voice, streamed TTS replies, and an account-credit quota meter.
features.usage_evidence: ELEVENLABS_API_KEY present in ~/.aiur/.env and aiur/.env (names only). elevenlabs.* set in 0 of 68 configs (env fallback). No retained daemon log line names an ElevenLabs session; voice usage lives with the Stream Deck/dashboard surfaces, which I did not measure.
features.raw_rationale: Only the voice surfaces use it; it belongs in the Stream Deck/voice package.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Move with the voice/Stream Deck package; the daemon keeps no provider credential for it.

challenge.recommendation: keep server-held ElevenLabs credential boundary until voice decisions are made
challenge.note: eleven_labs/realtime.ex and eleven_labs/tts.ex serve both browser and deck paths; website/docs-app/apis/elevenlabs.md:3-22 specifies restricted server-held credentials. Moving provider calls into the sidecar would alter that boundary and does not remove code. If all voice is deliberately retired, cut the provider; otherwise package extraction needs a protected service contract. The original estimate already says zero net LOC saving.

features.name: rtk output-compression integration
features.description: Admission gate and savings reader for rtk, which rewrites agent shell output; refuses unless rtk excludes gh.
features.usage_evidence: agent.rtk.enabled set in 0 of 68 configs (default false).
features.raw_rationale: Opt-in feature never enabled; the docs measure its saving as command-dependent.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Delete rtk.ex, the schema and the analytics panel hook.

challenge.recommendation: cut dormant rtk gate and its documented config surface
challenge.note: The raw config census found agent.rtk.enabled in 0 of 68 configs and defaults false; src/lib/aiur/rtk.ex is an optional admission path. Removing it is a plausible small deletion, but verify no transient environment activation and delete schema/docs/tests together. The 241 estimate is lib only and should not be presented as measured total repository reduction.

features.name: Run telemetry recorder (writer, resource sampler, lifecycle events, retention)
features.description: Daemon-owned NDJSON stream <run-log>/log/telemetry.ndjson: lifecycle phase events per ticket attempt (dispatch, prewarm, workspace_setup, workspace_ownership, agent_spinup, implement, build_test, review_pause, pr_opened, pr_merged, comment_received), procfs resource samples of daemon and agent process trees, sampler warnings, capacity holds, firehose polls, restarts; size/age retention and segment roll.
entry_points: Aiur.RunTelemetry.Lifecycle.record/5 (13 call sites in orchestrator, agent_runner, workspace/provisioner, coding_agent)
config: observability.telemetry_enabled, telemetry_retention_max_bytes (64 MiB), telemetry_retention_max_age_days (30), telemetry_retention_prune_interval_bytes
features.usage_evidence: Fires in every run: 34 of 39 retained run dirs (~/.aiur/logs/*/log/telemetry.ndjson, 2026-09-15..09-26) hold 454 MB. Record census (python over all files): 457,706 kind=resource, 434,147 kind=warning (243,151 ticket_roots_unavailable + 191,003 resource_sample_warning), 17,880 lifecycle, 3,247 firehose_poll, 42 restart, 9 capacity_hold, 7 capacity_resumed. So 97.6% of records are resource samples or sampler warnings; lifecycle is 2%. Largest file 57 MB, all under the 64 MiB cap (retention works). Consumers: the Executor reads the raw file directly (grep 'telemetry.ndjson' in Executor tool uses, excluding code-reading commands: 93 commands in 25 transcript files, mostly dispatch/lifecycle/resource greps); 14 Codex agent sessions also read it; the /analytics dashboard page (via subsystems-02) is observed in 79 of 173 aiur-team meta files. merged-fixes area N: run_telemetry/writer.ex touched by 4 daemon-stability fixes.
features.raw_rationale: Lifecycle phase timings are the one dataset the Executor actually greps, and they are cheap. The procfs sampler and its warnings produce ~98% of the bytes and nearly all of the noise (ticket_roots_unavailable fires every sample for every ticket whose workspace is not running). Keep the lifecycle writer + retention; cut per-process procfs sampling to a coarse host sample (load/mem) or drop it, and never persist per-sample warnings.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Remove Procfs (312) and most of Sampler (841); keep Writer + Retention with one schema. Emit warnings as counters in a periodic summary record, not one line per miss. Consider making lifecycle events the only telemetry and deriving capacity/firehose facts from them.

challenge.note:
The recommendation does not hold, because its central factual claim is wrong. The Python reducer is not an unused second copy. The daemon calls it automatically, and the dashboard reads what it writes.

1. The daemon calls it. src/lib/aiur/run_telemetry/summaries.ex does not write run-summary.json itself. The moduledoc says: "The canonical reducer is the `analytics/` Python package: this module invokes `analytics/reduce`". `reduce_command/1` builds `<dir>/reduce --all --all-builds --telemetry … --state-node …` and runs it with System.cmd. It looks for the directory in `RepoBase.base_path(repo)/analytics` (the `latest/` warm clone) and then in `./analytics`. There are two call sites:
   - writer.ex:324 calls `Summaries.materialize_async()` on every telemetry segment boundary.
   - writer.ex:165 calls `Summaries.materialize()` in `terminate/2` on daemon shutdown.
   The author searched Executor and agent transcripts. A call made by the daemon does not show up in either.

2. It has real output. On disk there are 21 run-summary.json files: 20 under ~/.aiur/repo/aiur-team/aiur/analytics/runs and 1 under architecture-docs. Every one has provenance.generated_by == "analytics/reduce" (the value that reduce.py:209 sets). They date from 2026-08-09 to 2026-09-22. There are also 10 build-summary.json files, the newest from 2026-09-21. These are written by `reduce --build`, which is the only writer (reduce.py:920).

3. Other code reads that output:
   - Analytics.Presenter.cross_session uses `Summaries.load_prior_datasets` for every prior boot.
   - LatestRun.load (presenter.ex:83) uses it for the latest-run view after a restart. It is also used by the `aiur analytics` CLI (AgentControlCLI.analytics → AnalyticsCLI) and by the Build Order analytics pane.
   - presenter.ex:186 branches on generated_by == "analytics/reduce".
   - mix aiur.cost_report (cost_report.ex:167) falls back to builds/<slug>/build-summary.json for build members.
   - docs concepts/build-orders.md:57 documents `analytics/runs/<boot-id>/run-summary.json` as a state-node path.

   What cutting it alone would break:
   - No new summaries would be written.
   - The latest-run view could no longer show the previous run after a restart. It shows `no_telemetry` instead.
   - The cross-session view would fall back to a full parse of the raw log.
   - Build rollups would stop.
   - `cost_report --build` would lose its fallback source.
   - The required CI `analytics` job (ci.yml:544) runs the unittest suite. Also, scripts/test-report-ci-failures.sh:98 uses the line `^  analytics:$` as the end of a sed range, so deleting that job breaks that guard.

4. The duplication point is still valid, but it is a different duplication than the one the author named. Python reduce.py (979 lines) is a parity port of the Elixir `Dataset.build` (dataset.ex, 1264 lines): summaries.ex `decode_summary` converts its JSON back into the Dataset shape. There is also a portability defect. The npm package `files` list does not include analytics/, so materialization only works on the dogfood host, where the aiur warm clone or the working directory contains analytics/. For product users it quietly does nothing, because it fails open.

   The right action is merge:
   - Have Summaries.materialize serialize the output of `Dataset.build` with Jason in Elixir, and add the build rollup there too.
   - Then delete the Python package, the run-summary, build-report and flake-report wrappers, and the CI job.
   - Fix the test-report-ci-failures.sh sed range.
   - Keep `mix aiur.cost_report` and delete only its 11-line shell shim.
   - Keep or move schema/run-summary.v1.json as the contract for the Elixir writer.

   These parts of the recommendation are correct:
   - flake-report is a stub: 43 lines plus a 7-line wrapper. Cut it.
   - Operators have not run run-summary or build-report by hand. The only Executor tool uses are one 2026-08-22 review session (8989d0ab) that edited reduce.py and ran its tests.

5. The LOC figure is right. The lib has 2071 lines of .py across 9 files. The 5 wrappers add 36 lines and the 2 schemas add 139, for 2246 in total. Tests (799 lines), fixtures and the 103-line README are not counted. The checked-in Elixir fixtures under src/test/fixtures/analytics/{runs,builds} were produced by the Python reducer. They encode its output contract, so they need to be regenerated by the Elixir writer after a merge.

challenge.note:
I could not refute the merge. Part of the author's reasoning is wrong, but the real evidence makes the case for the merge stronger.

(1) The stated reason is wrong. In a census of 6 non-private ledgers (13,457 records), cost is null in 98-100% of records, but tokens are greater than 0 in about 100% of them. The ledger holds token counts, and cost is computed later from PriceTable (usage/grouped_scopes/price_adapter.ex). So "cost is null" is no reason to lower durability.

The ledger's downstream readers go through UsageAggregate. They are documented and user-facing:
- dashboard_live (GroupedScopes USD)
- analytics_live
- aiur_web/build_order/usage_runtime.ex, the Build Order "this build" cost view
- financial_data/change_bridge
- mix aiur.cost_report

A merge must keep the aggregate query API. The one writer is Usage.Headless.Emitter, called from agent_runner/message_handler.ex. Claude REPL telemetry goes only to PubSub. No .aiur/config key, skill or doc page names the ledger. The only transcript hits are from this research session.

(2) "Regular use" is overstated because the ledger is saturated and has silently stopped recording.
- Store.capacity/4 returns :capacity_exhausted when the encoded checkpoint is larger than max_checkpoint_bytes = 1,048,576 (recovery.ex:10).
- CounterPolicy.idempotency is a MapSet that is never pruned.
- UsageLedger.retire keeps the counter state by design, so it can never free checkpoint space.
- Emitter.append discards the error, and nothing outside the ledger reads UsageLedger.health.

On disk:
- 7 of the 9 populated ledgers have checkpoint.json between 1,048,191 and 1,048,423 bytes, which is within 385 bytes of the cap. This caps each instance at about 1,900-2,500 records.
- The main aiur instance 539163312d recorded its last usage on 2026-07-30, but its other state kept updating until 2026-09-22.
- khala 95978a6838 stopped on 2026-09-18 while the instance stayed active until 2026-09-26.
- Every usage-compaction/blocks directory is empty, and no retired.json exists anywhere, so compaction and retirement have never run.
- The author's count is also slightly off: 9 of 14 dirs have data, not 10. The other 5 have 230-byte checkpoints and empty segments.

Result: the dashboard and Build Order cost figures stopped at the point of saturation. The recovery, quarantine and checkpoint machinery did not prevent this failure; its 1 MiB checkpoint cap caused it.

(3) Invariants the merged log must keep:
- Counter-to-delta derivation with epochs. Counter scope is "thread" for about 40% of Codex records (cumulative counters), so replaying without CounterPolicy would double-count.
- Idempotency by the envelope key.
- A bounded idempotency window, which is the fix for the bug above.
- A visible health signal.

An append-only log whose rollup is rebuilt by replay on boot can derive all of these. At 5-6 MB per instance, that replay is cheap.

LOC and attribution are correct: 1,790 lib lines in 8 modules. The raw wc output lists usage_ledger.ex twice, so its 1,902 total overcounts by 112. There are 1,626 test lines under test/aiur/usage_ledger, and 11 test files reference UsageLedger. Git history has 2 commits, both on 2026-07-17 (#1204, #1250), and nothing has changed since.

challenge.note:
I could not refute "merge". The rewrite notes are too lossy, though, and three claims in the evidence are wrong.

1. **Use.** No .aiur/config key, repo config, skill or sibling repo (khala, archon, aiur-claude) reads usage-aggregate. The Executor transcript hits are agents reading the code, not operators using the feature. The only callers are the ones listed, plus FinancialData.ChangeBridge (subscribes to the change topic) and UsageCompaction.Block (reuses Key and Projection).
   - The "79/173 meta files" figure counts the whole Analytics page. Most of that page is other telemetry. Of 176 meta .md files, only 9 mention the tile this feature feeds ("Provider spend"). About 5 of them say "not available", an em dash or "unavailable". None mention "Usage and cost" or the aggregate.
   - The aiur-meta capture test does treat "Usage and cost unavailable" on the Build Order page as an error. So the query surface must stay; the separate store does not have to.

2. **Correction: Query is test-only.** `UsageAggregate.Query` (188 LOC, reached through `UsageAggregate.query/1`) has no production caller; only query_test and store_test call it. Every real consumer goes through `cells_snapshot` and GroupedScopes, or reads the checkpoint file offline. The listed entry point "Query via GroupedScopes, usage_runtime, cost_report" is wrong.

3. **Merge conditions.** The merge is safe only if the rewrite keeps these:
   - **Wider key.** The proposed key {run, ticket, model} drops provider and upstream_provider. concepts/units.md documents "Cost by provider route" and says `mix aiur.cost_report --json` keeps provider and upstream_provider as separate fields.
   - **One Codex stream, or a stream field in the key.** The Codex turn and thread streams overlap; the thread_usage moduledoc says they are "not independently additive". In the live checkpoints they are about the same size: in the 199dc0ec57/aiur checkpoint, turn is 114.9M tokens and thread is 158.1M. relationship_revision keeps them in separate cells, but GroupedScopes `totals/2` adds them together anyway, so current totals already count Codex usage roughly twice. A key without the stream makes that double count permanent unless subsystems-04 drops one stream first.
   - **Repository-qualified ticket keys**, with bare issue numbers still rejected (Scope).
   - **cost_report must read the ledger.** `mix aiur.cost_report` reads the aggregate checkpoint offline without the daemon, so it must switch to replaying the ledger NDJSON. It has 0 operational runs.

4. **Rebuilding on boot is cheap.** Each live ledger is one segment of 1.9k-2.4k records and 4-5.5 MB. The checkpoints hold only 190-450 cells.

5. **Finding for subsystems-05: the ledgers appear full.** The ledger caps its checkpoint at 1,048,576 bytes (`@default_max_bytes`) and returns `:capacity_exhausted` above it (usage_ledger/store.ex around line 240). Six active instances have checkpoints between 1,048,191 and 1,048,423 bytes. That strongly suggests every one of them has stopped accepting records. On 539163312d/aiur, the ledger and aggregate both stopped on 2026-09-16, but other files there changed until 2026-09-22. So "regular" usage overstates how fresh the data is, and the aggregate's own checkpoint and recovery protect data that is not changing. This makes the case for the merge stronger.

6. **LOC.** 1,387 lib lines is correct. Tests are 597 lines, plus a 95-line support file. The ~1,000-line saving is plausible: Store, Checkpoint, Recovery, Paths, the Key codec and the dead Query come to about 1,000 lines. But GroupedScopes (904 LOC), PriceAdapter and Scope import Key and must be re-keyed.

challenge.note:
I could not refute it. The cut holds, and the case is stronger than the author's reason: in production compaction can never fire.

(1) Usage. There are 14 `usage-compaction` dirs under `~/.config/aiur` (the claim says 11). Across all of them there are 0 files, 0 `manifest.json`, 0 blocks, and 0 `usage-ledger/retired.json`. `grep compaction` over `<local-checkouts>/*/.aiur/config` finds nothing. No config key, docs page, skill or CLI command names it. The only production caller of `UsageLedger.retire/1` is the Coordinator, and nothing calls `Coordinator.snapshot/compact` outside its own tests. The 4 agent transcripts that mention it only list the test file in a test-partition run.

(2) Why it cannot fire. `aiur.ex:412` supervises the bare module with no opts, so `raw_bytes_fun` keeps its default `fn -> 0 end`. The byte trigger is therefore dead. The only live trigger is ledger position > 5,000 (`max_retained_positions`). The real ledgers top out at 2,553 positions (range 718-2,553; 6 are empty). They cannot reach 5,000: the ledger refuses appends with `:capacity_exhausted` when `checkpoint.json` reaches 1 MiB. 8 of the 14 checkpoints are already 1,048,191-1,048,423 bytes, which is 153-385 bytes below that 1,048,576-byte cap, at about 2,400 records.

The retire path does not relieve this cap. `store.ex` says retirement leaves the counter policy and checkpoint untouched and drops only raw segment lines. So the subsystem is unreachable by construction and does not target the constraint that actually binds. The rewrite must fix ledger checkpoint capacity separately. Compaction is not the tool for that.

(3) Invariants. No documented flow or safety invariant breaks. The subsystem is the only destructive seam, so removing it removes deletion risk. There is nothing on disk to migrate: no retired floor exists, so the ledger's retired-floor recovery branch is dead as well.

LOC attribution. The 1,297 lines in the 6 modules are correct but understate the cut. The cut also includes:
- `UsageLedger.RetiredFloor` (82 lines)
- `retire/commit_retirement` in `usage_ledger/store.ex`
- the retired-floor restore branch in `usage_ledger/recovery.ex`
- `UsageAggregate.Store.rebuild_from_floor`, which becomes plain `Projection.new`, plus `Projection.seed`
- `Config.Paths.usage_compaction_state_dir`
- 555 test lines in `test/aiur/usage_compaction`
- the supervision-order test at `application_test.exs:450`

challenge.note:
The "cut" rests on a misread of the data. The 1525 lib LOC figure is correct (test LOC is 1509). The envelope counts also reproduce exactly from the 9 non-empty ~/.config/aiur/*/*/usage-ledger segments: 12,056 codex, 5,400 claude and 1,133 deepseek. What the counts show is wrong, though.

(1) owner_unavailable does not mean the owner is down. It is Snapshot.unavailable/2 (snapshot.ex:22), which Usage.Headless.Context.account_generation/3 (context.ex:107-110) uses as the default when the caller supplies no :account_generation opt. Only open_ai_compat/coding_agent.ex:262-270 supplies one. So the 94% figure shows that the snapshot never reaches the Codex/Claude usage envelopes. That is a plumbing gap, not a dead subsystem.

(2) The owner is live and healthy on the meter path. ProviderMeters.Store.normalize_update/resolve_generation (store.ex:88-124) rejects every meter update that has no :healthy generation. Codex meters reach `aiur usage` (documented in cli.md:87), the TUI (render_state.ex:102), the dashboard and the Stream Deck only through Codex.AccountGeneration.handle_notification -> ProviderMeters.ingest. Executor transcript 31796d96 shows live `aiurdev usage` output that had to pass this gate: "codex:primary 11%", "codex_bengalfox:primary 0%" and "reset-credits $1.00" at 2026-09-02T07:07, and "codex:primary 33%" at 2026-09-03T03:48. The operator also made dispatch decisions from this meter ("codex:primary is at 100/100 weekly"). operating-aiur.md documents "Codex and Claude: Percentage used in renewing allotment windows".

(3) Codex.AccountGeneration (312 LOC) does more than mint generations:
- It routes account/rateLimits/updated to ExhaustedReset, the Codex usage-limit pause shipped in #2742 on 2026-09-18.
- It feeds ModelAvailability.observe through rate_limit_observer, the rate-limit fallback. That feed runs only when the meter accepts the reading.
- It is the privacy redaction for account/* notifications. It swaps them for content-free provider_account/* messages with raw: nil. codex/notifications.ex:38-50 and session_lifecycle.ex:22 otherwise emit the raw payload into the message and log stream.

The rewrite note says "Delete ProviderAccountGeneration.* and the three backend context modules". Doing that would break the Codex meters and the #2742 reset feed, and would remove the account-payload redaction invariant.

(4) The git evidence is stale. There are 5 commits, not 3, and the latest is #2742 on 2026-09-18, not 08-09.

Some of the criticism does hold:
- Claude's dashboard meter comes from Claude.UsageApi with generation nil (provider_meter_probe.ex:209-217). That makes Claude.AccountGeneration and the AccountMeters rate-limit ingest largely redundant.
- ProviderMeterProjection strips the generation (line 165). Its moduledoc admits that the binding-scoped dashboard read always fell back to unknown identity.
- The generic Owner/Registry/Lifecycle/Tombstones/Continuity machinery (about 800 LOC) is heavy for what is really a per-session auth epoch.

Recommended simplification:
- Replace the minting owner with a per-session auth epoch, or with a key of provider+backend+credential name, and keep the rule that readings from different accounts are never merged.
- Keep the Codex notification router with its redaction, the ExhaustedReset feed and the ModelAvailability feed.
- Drop the Claude generation path.
- Either pass the snapshot into the Codex/Claude usage envelopes or remove the field from the envelopes and from the pricing tier_join_key.

challenge.note:
The merge recommendation does not hold. Its rationale is wrong on the facts, and folding this subsystem into the registry would undo a deliberate design boundary.

1) Real use the author missed:
- ~/.aiur/model-catalog.json is refreshed daily. On 2026-09-25 it held claude with 6 ids and codex with 5 ids. The codex list includes gpt-6-astra, which is NOT in the curated registry list at coding_agent.ex:104-112. gpt-6-astra is also the operator's own Codex default (per a khala-13 workspace transcript).
- Discovery is the only reason aiur accepts gpt-6-astra and resolves the family alias `astra`. The path is CodingAgent.resolvable_ids/3, which appends ModelDiscovery.cached_models (coding_agent.ex:718). Without it, every `model:astra` or `codex:astra` ticket would get an unsupported_model / model_label_unresolved attention.
- The documented contract depends on it. website/docs-app/concepts/ticket-lifecycle.md ("Model labels", added by #2759 on 2026-09-24) uses `model:astra` and `model:codex-astra` as examples. It also says names "come from the installed CLIs, not from aiur" and that `aiur init` creates a `model:<family>` label for each family the CLIs report (init/labels.ex:92-132 → ModelCatalog.discover).

2) Documented flows and invariants that a merge would touch:
- The config key `agent.backend_configs.<backend>.model_discovery` is documented in reference/configuration.md ("Model discovery" section, around line 427-501), and that doc is enforced by check-config-docs.py.
- Discovery is on the hot path in several places:
  - Model-label resolution runs on every orchestrator poll and must stay cache-only (coding_agent.ex:1093-1102).
  - SessionLifecycle.maybe_alert_unsupported_model (line 1012).
  - AgentRunner.ModelLabelRefresh refreshes the cache before labels are resolved.
  - The OCC routing preview (agent_routing_preview.ex:102).
  - OpenAICompat.Registry wires Source.OpenAI and Source.OpenRouter as `models_endpoint`.
- The moduledoc sets out invariants on purpose: nothing writes to the registry, curated metadata wins, config validation makes no network call, and fetched prices never flow into the PriceTable.
- CodingAgent is a curated data registry and is already 1392 lines. Merging a network, cache and file-locking subsystem into it would blur exactly those boundaries.
- The subsystem is not stale. #2759 (2026-09-24, 1661 lines added) just made it the backbone of release-proof model labels.

3) LOC and attribution:
- The 1287 lines for the 6 listed files is correct.
- The feature footprint is understated. It leaves out agent_runner/model_label_refresh.ex (149), coding_agent/model_label.ex (114), the discovery path in init/labels.ex, and about 794 lines of tests.
- "Three discovery sources" is inaccurate. Source.Anthropic (48 lines) is wired to no backend; its own moduledoc says "No registry backend declares this source today". It is reached only from model_discovery_test.exs.
- The HTTP provider path is cold. The deepseek cache entry was last fetched 2026-09-03, and there is no cached entry for openrouter or kimi. The live path is the CLI model/list probe (ModelCatalog).
- Routing is not "a list the operator configures by hand". The operator's configs use family aliases that are resolved against the discovered set: codex:luna/terra/sol (kevinweaver-dev), claude:sonnet/opus (~/.aiur/config).

Recommended action: keep it as its own subsystem and simplify it.
- Cut the unwired Source.Anthropic adapter, its tests, and the doc sentence about it.
- Consider trimming the advisory OpenRouter price-drift and unpriced-model reporting. It only fires on the cold HTTP path.
- Do not merge it into the backend registry.

Privacy correction (2026-09-26): private configuration values removed; the public configuration examples above are sufficient evidence for this recommendation.

challenge.note:
I could not refute it, and the cut holds. Readers: grep over the snapshot's src, scripts, .claude, website, packaging and analytics finds only the writer (src/lib/aiur/operator_wait_log.ex), the supervisor child (src/lib/aiur.ex:425), two call sites (src/lib/aiur/orchestrator/operator_messages.ex:997 and :1031), one comment (src/lib/aiur/opencode/chat_completions/operator_dispatch.ex:31) and tests. The analytics/ reducers do not read metrics/. No sibling repo under <local-checkouts>/everdred and no .aiur/config reads it; the only other hits are aiur worktree copies and an erl_crash.dump. In ~/.claude/projects/*aiur*, the only transcripts that mention operator_message_wait are this research session's own, so Executor reads are 0. On disk the file is in 13 of 39 run dirs under ~/.aiur/logs, with 1 to 38 lines each.

The author missed docs/, which the snapshot left out. Four places there name the log, but none is a reader or a user doc: (a) docs/refactor/feature-inventory/art.md FI-ART-020 and orc.md FI-ORC-075, from the 2026-07 "no feature is removed" anti-regression contract. The rewrite must retire those IDs on purpose. (b) docs/operator-control-center/02-occ-0-audit-and-design-decisions.md:25, which says only the provider receipt closes the OperatorWaitLog interval. (c) Two old plans in docs/plans.

Invariant: the safety property in (b) is that queued and provider-delivered stay distinct. The transcript events next to each call carry it: status :queued with request_id, then status :delivered with request_id, provider_turn_id and provider_delivered_at. That is also why the wait can still be worked out from agent.ndjson. Cutting the module breaks neither that property nor any documented flow.

Two more points for the cut: (1) The moduledoc says samples "accumulate across runs for trend analysis". That is stale: the log root is per run (~/.aiur/logs/<ts>-<pid>/log/metrics/), and decision_metrics_restart_test.exs asserts that operator-wait metrics stay run-local. (2) record_queued adds an ETS row that only record_delivered removes, so a message that is never delivered leaves its row there until restart.

LOC: 116 lib lines is correct. The full cut also removes src/test/aiur/operator_wait_log_test.exs (91 lines), about 4 lines of alias, calls and child, and the two OperatorWaitLog assertions in decision_metrics_restart_test.exs. Edit that test rather than delete it, because it also guards DecisionMetrics. Keep Aiur.Metrics, which DecisionMetrics shares.

challenge.note:
The recommendation does not hold. Its usage evidence is misattributed, its footer claim is stale, and its merge target is a poor fit.

(1) Usage is misattributed. All 4,767 aiur_perf lines in the 3 retained ~/.aiur/logs/*/log/aiur.log files come from plain Logger.info("aiur_perf ...") calls outside Aiur.Perf. The breakdown is 4,510 github_firehose (comment_polling.ex), 94 workspace_hook (workspace/hooks.ex), 85 ls_remote_ticker, and the dispatcher.ex hold lines (prewarm_hold, load_hold, envelope_hold). Zero lines have the Perf.format_line shape "aiur_perf phase=". The Executor's aiur_perf use in transcripts (github_quota_hold, prewarm_hold, phase_stagger_hold) and the tests that assert line text (dispatcher_test, build_gate_test on memory_hold, fd_hold, prewarm_hold and phase_stagger_hold) also cover those non-Perf lines. So the tested, operational contract is the "aiur_perf" prefix used by the dispatcher and build gates, not this module. Aiur.Perf's own output has no observed use. Its phase= lines appear in ~/.aiur only inside copied repo docs.

(2) "Feeds the debug footer" is stale. AgentList.App subscribes to Perf.topic() in debug mode, and PerfIntake folds events into perf_summary and warmth_events. render_state.ex passes both along, but no renderer module (agent_list/renderer/*) reads them, so this consumer is dead. PerfIntake also folds :placeholder_spawn_done, but PaneManager.Placeholder only emits it through span_begin(:placeholder_spawn), so that path has to stay in sync by hand. Opencode.WarmthReport, the parser for this line shape, has no callers in lib, only tests. The perf_regression tests that parse aiur.log are excluded by default (test_helper.exs). Some of them match phases nothing emits any more (attach_pool_warm, slot_chain_parallel_start).

(3) Merging into RunTelemetry.Lifecycle conflicts with that module's contract. Lifecycle has a closed list of 14 @events, a sanitized metadata allowlist, and a telemetry_enabled? gate. Perf has about 60 free-form pane and opencode phases and is always on. The 2026-06-14 logging-observability plan says "always-on aiur_perf lines ... gating happens at the handler".

(4) Scope and history. The 104 LOC figure is right, but the footprint is 85 Perf.event and span calls across 20 lib files, plus PerfIntake and WarmthReport, which are both dead. The PubSub topic is still a test seam: convo_paint_test and shared_prewarm_e2e_test use assert_receive {:aiur_perf, ...}. Git history has 2 commits (d8d167a08 2026-05-22 #65, then the 2026-06-02 rename), not 1. No config keys, docs pages or skills refer to it.

Action: simplify. Keep a single structured-log helper for the "aiur_perf <name> k=v" convention, which the dispatcher and build-gate lines and their tests already depend on. Drop the PubSub broadcast, PerfIntake, WarmthReport and the stale perf_regression log tests. Rewrite the two PubSub-seam tests against real effects, and do not fold these phases into RunTelemetry.

challenge.note:
The line count is right: 243+605+13+532+151 = 1544. Usage is real. I found 6 live checkpoints under ~/.config/aiur/<key>/<repo>/progress-retention/checkpoint.json, sized 8-169 KB (khala written 2026-09-26, aiur 2026-09-19). The brief placed them in ~/.aiur, which is wrong. The merge premise does not hold: the three modules do not hold one fact.

(1) ProgressTracker has no ETS and no process. It is a set of pure helpers (record/estimate/bar/format_eta), and its sample list lives in AgentList state (agent_list/activity_intake.ex:121, renderer/cells.ex:92-101). Its moduledoc ("ETS-backed sample store") is stale. The ETA path is dead: no lib file uses eta_seconds or format_eta, only test/aiur/progress_tracker_test.exs. So no "ETA column" exists. The live part keeps a rate-projected percent capped at 99 for the TUI bar. It is a renderer helper, not a second copy of the progress fact.

(2) ProgressRetention is separate from TicketActivity on purpose, and a merge breaks invariants that tests guard:
- StatusReport reads ProgressRetention.all/0 directly from its own ETS mirror (status_report.ex:731-775). It uses this as a fallback for exactly the case where TicketActivity times out, crashes or has not reseeded.
- If the store merges into the TicketActivity process, a projection crash destroys the ETS mirror and the in-memory retained map. The fallback then reports unknown, and readings still inside the 2 s debounce window are lost.
- This conflicts with the documented Stream Deck contract "Unknown = No reading has ever arrived" (guide/stream-deck.md:62) and its note that a bar that drops to an empty track and back is a bug.
- Guarding tests: status_report_test.exs:283 and :349 (#1963), and application_test.exs:487-491, which asserts that ProgressRetention is supervised and starts before TicketActivity under the :rest_for_one Aiur.Supervisor (aiur.ex:115, :433-436).

(3) TicketActivity/Projection holds more than progress: stage, latest safe evidence, current/recent membership retention, diagnostics and the PubSub broadcast. About 12 lib files consume it (agent_list, build_order, current_run_projections, status_report, dashboard_live, OCC units_presenter, stream_deck_grid).

Recommended simplification:
- Fold the 13-line Reducer into Projection.
- Delete ProgressTracker's dead ETA code (compute_eta, format_eta, the eta_seconds field) and fix its moduledoc, or move bar/estimate into agent_list/renderer/cells.ex.
- Keep ProgressRetention as its own supervised store with an independent ETS mirror.

No config key, skill or docs quick start names these modules. The merge risk is in the invariant, not in external references.

challenge.note:
I could not refute the cut. Only the stated reason is weak.

Usage and breakage are confirmed.
- I counted 33 retained daemon logs under ~/.aiur/logs: 3 'armed', 236 'entered', 236 'disarmed' and 569 'record_failed' lines.
- Every record_failed line is the same Protocol.UndefinedError from Jason.Encoder on {:total, N}. The cause is in snapshot/1: `memory: safe(&:erlang.memory/0)` returns a keyword list of tuples, and Jason cannot encode tuples, so record/2 has failed on every call since it landed (394f81779, 2026-08-09).
- I found 0 saturation.log files under ~/.aiur, ~/.config/aiur or the repos.
- The unit test did not catch this because its fixture is a hand-made map with no :memory key (test/aiur/saturation_sentinel_test.exs:73). This is the "fixture built to avoid the failure mode" shape that AGENTS.md warns about.

Hidden consumers: none found.
- No live .aiur/config sets agent.saturation_log_enabled. One private repo has it as a commented-out line only.
- The agent schema does not reject unknown keys (only the polling schema does), so removing the field cannot break a config that still sets it.
- No skill or guide page reads saturation.log.
- scripts/aiur-saturation-repro.sh:281-294 tails the file only when `[ -f ]` finds it, so the block becomes dead but harmless.
- About 30 transcripts mention the module, but all of them are file listings, supervisor-child dumps or record_failed log greps. None consumes the output.
- The 2026-08-03 saturation root-cause measurement doc that described it is no longer in the snapshot.

Invariants: the module is fail-open diagnostics and guards nothing. Its only working output is the entered/disarmed Logger lines (load1, schedulers, threshold). RunTelemetry.Sampler already records the same data every 5 s as fleet_load, fleet_load_threshold and fleet_schedulers (sampler.ex:23, 330-332).

Correction to the rationale: "covered by crash dumps" is contradicted by the module's own moduledoc. It says the #852 dump was sparse, and that is why the module was built. The accurate reason to cut is:
- its unique output (BEAM process, port, atom, ETS and run-queue counts) has never been written in production;
- its working output repeats what RunTelemetry already records.

If crash diagnosability under saturation still matters, the rewrite should add those few BEAM counters to the RunTelemetry sample rather than keep a separate 245-line GenServer. Reviving it would take a one-line fix (Map.new(:erlang.memory())), which is a reason not to call it hard to fix, but not a reason to keep it.

LOC and attribution: correct. lib/aiur/saturation_sentinel.ex is 245 lines. A full cut also removes:
- the 97-line test file;
- the schema field in config/schema/agent.ex:240-245 and :316;
- Config.saturation_log_enabled?/0 (config.ex:793-800);
- the supervisor child in aiur.ex:312;
- the docs row at configuration.md:245 (scripts/check-config-docs.py enforces this row);
- optionally, the repro-script tail block.

challenge.note:
I could not refute the cut. Every check below points the same way.

(1) Consumers. In the snapshot at 3339b887, only two places refer to the module: the supervisor child at src/lib/aiur.ex:311 and its own test, src/test/aiur/agent_process_log_test.exs (343 lines). The agent_process_group_id hits in codex/claude/session_lifecycle are an unrelated metadata key. No doc, skill, script, analytics file or .aiur/config under <local-checkouts>/everdred/* mentions agent-processes, AgentProcessLog or even the github-quota/ directory. Outside the TSV files themselves, nothing under ~/.aiur refers to them.

Claude transcripts: every tool call that touched the log came from session 8989d0ab on 2026-08-22/23, reviewing PR #2295 for a credential leak (denylist replaced by an allowlist). The other hits are agents reading the aiur.ex child list. No Executor ever read the TSV for an operational question.

Codex rollouts: about 17 agent sessions between 09-03 and 09-24 hit the TSVs, but only as noise in broad `grep -r ~/.aiur` searches for guard-pr-deletions. That is a negative. The files waste agent context, and their cwd and ticket columns show one repo's workspace paths and ticket numbers to agents working in other repos.

(2) Invariants. Nothing breaks. application_test only checks declared-vs-running child order and does not name this child. RequestLog, quota.ex and the gh guard do not call it. The pid join to agent-requests.tsv is manual analysis described only in the moduledoc. Cutting it also removes an argv-to-disk writer that has already needed a security rework, and one child from a :rest_for_one supervisor.

(3) Attribution. 576 lib lines is correct; add the 343-line test. The usage claim understates what is on disk: "6.4 MB total" counts only the active files. With rotated generations it is 24 files, 82.4 MB, across the 5 repos. The rotation cap is about 36 MiB per repo, and the files sit outside Logs.Retention, so dormant repos (archon, architecture-docs) keep theirs indefinitely. Cut action: delete src/lib/aiur/agent_process_log.ex, its test and the aiur.ex:311 child. Then do a one-time cleanup of ~/.aiur/repo/*/*/github-quota/agent-processes.tsv*, because nothing will prune those files once the writer is gone.

features.name: Agent resource guard (trim synthetic load generators)
features.description: Watches registered agent process roots and kills known load-generator descendants (yes/stress) above a cap.
features.usage_evidence: Active by default (synthetic_load_process_cap null = cores/4; the key appears only as a commented template line in the home config and 12 of 12 home-config backups, uncommented in 0 of 7 configs). Trims observed: 0 log lines mentioning resource_guard/synthetic load in retained aiur.log/boot.out.log. git: 1 commit (2026-06-23).
features.raw_rationale: Guards against one historical agent behaviour; no trims observed.

challenge.note:
The "no use" part holds, and the evidence for it is stronger than the author's. The cut does not hold as stated, because it removes a default-on safety backstop that came from a real incident, and its reason ("no trims observed") is weak for a guard whose normal state is not firing. Merging the guard into an existing observer keeps the safety check at about 30 lines.

USAGE: none found, confirmed with a better census.
- The AgentProcessLog files (`~/.aiur/repo/*/*/github-quota/agent-processes.tsv*`: 24 rotated files, 5 repos) record every agent subprocess. From 2026-08-23 to 2026-09-26 they hold 250,963 subprocess starts and 0 with comm yes, stress or stress-ng.
- No `trimmed_synthetic_load` line appears in retained logs. Those logs only cover about 2026-09-15 to 09-20 (3 aiur.log files), so the author's log evidence alone was thin.
- None of the 99 retained workspace agent transcripts ran a load generator.
- No real trim line appears in `~/.claude/projects`.
- GitHub has one incident only: #479 (2026-06-23). An agent spawned 16 `yes` workers on the 12-core box, load reached 45, and 8 sibling agents starved. No recurrence was found.
- The config key appears only as a commented template line (aiur `.aiur/examples/config.example:47`, the home config, and 2 other repo configs). It is set in 0 configs.

WHAT A CUT BREAKS OR FORCES:
1. It drops the only runtime enforcement of #479's R1-R3 ("one agent's yes/stress repro cannot drive host load unboundedly"). The guard is default-on (nil means max(1, cores/4)). It is listed as FI-CFG-055, Risk: high, in the anti-regression inventory (`docs/refactor/feature-inventory/cfg.md`), and `docs/refactor/research-history-hotspots.md` §7 names #479/PR #503 as an archetype resource-exhaustion case. The prompt rule in `.claude/skills/aiur-agent/conventions.md:78-84` is the real mitigation today (agents cite it, e.g. an #1684 comment), but it is advice, not enforcement.
2. Another feature's test depends on the guard: `src/test/aiur/orchestrator_deactivate_test.exs:6868` uses `AgentResourceGuard.collect_descendants/1` as a helper. The twin in `RemoteControl` (`remote_control.ex:427`) is `defp`, so a cut must expose a replacement.
3. A cut must also remove the schema field and validation (`config/schema/agent.ex:235,314,343`), `Config.synthetic_load_process_cap` and its default helper (`config.ex:~930-955`), the docs row (`website/docs-app/reference/configuration.md:240`), the example template line, the child entries in `aiur.ex:310` and `application_test.exs:110`, and the config test (`workspace_and_config_test.exs:2619`). Ecto cast ignores unknown keys, so a user config that still sets the key will not fail to parse.

LOC AND ATTRIBUTION: the 192 lib lines are correct. The feature also owns 105 test lines, about 25 lines of config glue, and the doc and template lines. `ProcessReaper.entries/0` cannot be deleted with it, because `AgentProcessLog` (line 437) and `RunTelemetry.Sampler` (line 54) also use it.

WHY MERGE AND NOT KEEP:
- The guard is costly: every 1s it runs a recursive `pgrep -P` fork for every node in every agent tree. That adds load on the host it protects.
- It duplicates tree walking already in `RemoteControl` and `ProcessReaper` (`docs/refactor/research-arch/dup-infra.md` §6).
- Its coverage is partial:
  - It reads only `{:os_pid, _}` entries of kind `:agent`. Opencode agents register only `{:pane, _}` refs, so they are not covered.
  - Generators that are backgrounded or reparented leave the tree and escape.
  - It matches by name only, so other CPU burners (for example a shell `while :` loop) pass.
  - It reads `/proc`, so it does nothing on macOS.
- `AgentProcessLog` already takes one `ps -eo` snapshot every 2s and walks each registered agent root in memory (`agent_process_log.ex:191-244,454-501`). The yes/stress check and the trim should run as a small policy on that snapshot. This keeps the #479 check and the documented key, and deletes the separate GenServer, the duplicate pgrep walk and the 1 Hz fork cost.

If the rewrite still cuts the guard, it must record a waiver for FI-CFG-055, keep the `conventions.md` prompt rule, and ideally replace the guard with a per-agent cgroup CPU quota. That quota was the "most robust" fix direction in #479 and covers every CPU burner, not only named ones.

features.name: Pause containment (agent process-group registration for pause/stop)
features.description: Registers each agent's root pid and process group with a generation; confirm/release/paused? during cooperative pause; liveness polling.
features.usage_evidence: Registered at every agent spawn (6 call-site modules). Retained daemon logs contain 71 containment lines, all 'Orchestrator ignored message: {:pause_containment_runtime, ...}' - the runtime notification has no handler.
features.raw_rationale: A second pid/pgid registry beside ProcessReaper; its runtime message is dropped by the orchestrator.
features.raw_rewrite_notes: Fold into the process-group registry of subsystems-30.

challenge.note:
The merge recommendation does not hold. The module is a live safety path, and it is not a duplicate of ProcessReaper.

(1) It kills agents in production. The daemon alert feeds (~/.aiur/logs/*/log/*alerts.ndjson) hold 17 `ticket.N.agent.pause.cooperative` arms and 8 `agent.pause.fallback_succeeded` reaps across 3 runs (20260916T190631Z, 20260916T212437Z, 20260917T022859Z). Each of those 8 was an agent that ignored a cooperative pause and was stopped when its process group was killed ("Recorded agent process group contained."). A grep over all logs finds 174 cooperative, 45 fallback_started and 45 fallback_succeeded lines, with duplicates across the github-*.log files. The 71 "Orchestrator ignored message" lines are only one side-channel. The real output is Alerts.emit_system plus the reap itself.

(2) The dropped message does not belong to this module. `{:pause_containment_runtime, ...}` is sent by AgentRunner.SessionLifecycle.report_pause_containment (src/lib/aiur/agent_runner/session_lifecycle.ex:51-62). PauseContainment's own `{:pause_containment_result, ...}` (pause_containment.ex:350-356, notify_orchestrator) also has no handler: orchestrator.ex:238 is the catch-all. Both are dead wiring and can be cut. The core functions do not depend on them:
- `arm` is called from orchestrator/pause_resume.ex:1822.
- `arm_target` is called from agent_control_cli.ex:1413. This is an independent fallback when the orchestrator is congested or times out.
- `confirm` is called from agent_runner/turn_loop.ex:172.
- `paused?` is a per-turn latch in codex/turn_loop.ex:218 and app_server/adapter.ex:153.
- `release_target` is called from queue_drain.ex, agent_runner.ex and pause_resume.ex.

(3) Merging into ProcessReaper would break invariants:
- ProcessReaper kills synchronously inside its GenServer. See `handle_call({:reap,...})`, the draining register-kill path, and the 25s call timeout. PauseContainment reaps off-loop on purpose (#893 "Reap agent group off the containment loop") so that one slow TERM->KILL does not delay a sibling agent's pause. After a merge, `paused?` (1s timeout, catch -> :ignored -> false) would fail open while a reap runs, and the turn loop would continue a paused agent.
- The two modules use different kill primitives. PauseContainment calls killpg on a setsid group and refuses registration unless root_pid == pgid. ProcessReaper uses graceful_kill_tree with a /proc cmdline guard.
- They use different keys: identifier+generation with a fail-closed suffix match, against os_pid/pane.
- ProcessReaper registrations are turned off in test env (`:process_reaper_registrations`), which would disable containment in tests.
- Tests encode these contracts: build_gate_test.exs:1541 (#1154 build lock released after the containment reap), build_gate_test.exs:1564 (#2387/#2404: the containment reap spares adopted dbus/keyring daemons), and application_test.exs:212 (start order).

(4) Attribution is partly wrong. The 404 LOC and the single lib module are correct. "Registered at every agent spawn" is not: registration happens only for Codex app-server sessions, through Codex.SessionLifecycle.register_pause_containment (codex/coding_agent.ex:79). Claude, REPL and opencode spawns do not register. The 6 modules call the arm/confirm/paused?/release API, not register.

Nothing in website/docs-app or the skills documents this module (it is internal, with @moduledoc false).

Recommended action: keep the subsystem, but simplify it. Delete both unhandled notifications (report_pause_containment and notify_orchestrator/notify_fun). Collapse the duplicated register/confirm/release/paused?/unregister arity wrappers. Deduplicate the release/release_target clause bodies.

RepoBase also exports the per-repo state path helpers (repo_path/builds_path) used by 22 files.
entry_points: DispatchPolicy.prewarm_gate + dispatcher prewarm hold (~150 lines in orchestrator/dispatcher.ex)
features.usage_evidence: prewarm.enabled=true in 2 of 7 configs (aiur, kevinweaver-dev). Retained telemetry prewarm events: 22 materialize starts, 9 success, 13 materialize_failed -> cold fallback (59% failure), 430 'existing' skips, 89 'disabled'. aiur Executor wake stream: 1,015 system.dispatch.prewarm_blocked wakes between 2026-08-18 and 08-24. merged-fixes 2.17: 5-fix chain (#441, #571, #1555, #2274, #2434), disabled in #2242 (two starts stalled with 31 ready tickets and 0 agents), later re-enabled. Executor: 36 operational commands in 8 files. Note: pre_warmed_sessions (opencode pane prewarm, 7/7 configs) is a different feature owned by the TUI/opencode surface.
