challenge.note:
The cut does not hold. Each of its three reasons is either an artifact of a bug that was fixed on the same day, or a flood that stopped once its cause was fixed. The LOC attribution is also wrong in both directions.

(1) The 59% failure rate is one bug, not the design. All 13 `materialize_failed` events happened on 2026-09-16 between 15:37Z and 18:13Z. All 13 carry the same `reason_class`, `unexpected_crash_dump_path` (workspace/materialize.ex:103). #2651 fixed it at 18:35Z that day ("Preserve warm copies with embedded repositories"). After that fix, 9 of 9 materializations succeeded. Source: ~/.aiur/logs/*/log/telemetry.ndjson.

(2) The saving is measured, not estimated. Telemetry from the same runs gives aiur `workspace_setup` a median of 198.7s on cold fallback (n=12, p90 241s) and 26.7s when materialized (n=9, p90 34s). That is about 170s saved per new aiur workspace.

(3) The wake flood was a fixed defect. All 1,015 `system.dispatch.prewarm_blocked` wakes have `first_seen_at` between 08-18 and 08-24. They are blocked/resolved pairs (515/500) from #2237, where the `:checking` state never exited. #2274 (08-23) added the idle watchdog and turned prewarm back on in the same PR. #2434 made the alert fire only on holds that persist. After that:
- The aiur wake stream has no `prewarm_blocked` wakes from 08-24 to 09-20.
- Retained run alerts from 09-15 to 09-26 have none either.
- Prewarm stayed on the whole time.

(4) The #2242 disable was temporary. Its config comment says "Re-enable once #2237 lands", and it was re-enabled. HEAD `.aiur/config` has `enabled: true` and `poll_seconds: 30`. `~/.aiur/repo/aiur-team/aiur/base-record.json` was built on 09-19 at 0972f029.

(5) The proposed replacement already exists and is not enough. The shared deps cache is `RepoBase.cache_sidecar_paths` (`.aiur-hex`, `.aiur-mix`, `.aiur-npm-cache`). AgentEnvironment uses it for every repo, including khala and archon, where prewarm is off. Cold fallback already uses it and still takes about 200s. The missing piece is the warm `_build`, and that is exactly what the base supplies.

(6) The LOC and module attribution are wrong. Of repo_base.ex's 1,539 lines:
- About 130 are path helpers used by 22 files.
- About 650 (lines 793–1440) are state-tree migration: `ensure_state_tree` calls `migrate_legacy_layout`, which also merges the findings and asks ledgers. Findings, asks and hooks all call `ensure_state_tree`, so this code stays whatever happens to prewarm.

Warm-base code the survey left out:
- init/prewarm.ex (207 lines)
- init/prewarm/failure.ex (153)
- workspace/materialize.ex (106)
- the dispatcher gate, alert and watchdog (83 prewarm references)
- the prewarm branches in status_report, status_reason, state, issue_sync, provisioner and the agent_list loading bar

(7) It is documented. configuration.md has a prewarm section covering the watchdog and alert semantics. It also appears in quick-start ("Prepare state"), the cli.md `init` row, the ticket-lifecycle binding table, and the aiur-run SKILL check of `base-record.json`. 51 test files mention it.

Usage evidence is correct but narrow. Only aiur (and its clone checkouts) and kevinweaver-dev enable it, and the kevinweaver-dev base was last built on 08-03. In practice that means aiur alone, but aiur is the main dogfood workload.

Recommended simplification:
- Split RepoBase into a StatePaths/state-tree module (paths, sidecar caches, ledgers) and a separate WarmBase module.
- Stop holding the whole fleet while the base builds or probes. Dispatch cold until the base is ready. That removes the gate, the alert and the watchdog, which is where every incident started.
- Consider retiring the one-time legacy-layout migration once all nodes have migrated.

features.name: RTK output-compression admission
features.description: Opt-in gate that wraps agent shell commands with the `rtk` CLI and reads its savings.
features.usage_evidence: agent.rtk.* set in 0 of 7 real configs. Codex agent sessions executing 'rtk git|rtk gain': 0 (rg over ~/.codex/sessions); Claude agent transcripts containing 'rtk ': 0. Executor: 22 operational commands in 3 files, all 2026-09-03 while building it. git: 1 commit.
features.raw_rationale: Opt-in and never enabled.

challenge.note:
I could not refute the cut. The case is stronger than the brief says, because the "admission gate" gates nothing in the agent path.

1. Hidden use: none found.
- Callers: the only caller of Aiur.Rtk outside its own tests is AiurWeb.AnalyticsLive.rtk_panel/0 (analytics_live.ex:409). No module on the agent spawn, env or workspace path calls Rtk.status/1 or Rtk.enabled?/0.
- The moduledoc and commit ead845292 (#2521) both say it "never puts rtk on an agent's PATH and never installs the hook". So `agent.rtk.enabled: true` changes nothing about agent commands. It only switches the analytics card from "Output compression is off" to a probe.
- Docs: the configuration.md:218 claim "Opts agents into rtk output compression" is false today.
- Configs: `rtk` appears in 0 of 14 .aiur/config files, not 7. I checked every .aiur/config under <local-checkouts>/everdred at depth 3, plus ~/.aiur/config.
- Host state: rtk is installed at ~/.local/bin/rtk, but its Claude hook is not set up in ~/.claude/settings.json, the repo .claude/settings*.json, or ~/.codex/config.toml. ~/.local/share/rtk/history.db was last written 2026-09-02, the build day, so rtk has filtered nothing since.
- Transcripts: Claude transcripts that mention rtk commands are only the Sep 2–3 build session (31796d96) and this research workflow. Codex sessions: 0 files.
- Skills, quick starts and example workflows: no references.

2. Safety invariant: nothing breaks.
- The "gh must be excluded" check runs only when the flag is on and someone opens the analytics page. It never stops an rtk hook that an operator installed by hand from rewriting the gh quota guard. The invariant is displayed, not enforced, so cutting it loses no protection.
- Schema key: no config sets `agent.rtk`, so removing it breaks nothing.
- Docs: delete the configuration.md:218 row in the same PR so the reference does not describe a key that no longer exists.

3. LOC and attribution: the brief understates the footprint. rtk.ex has 241 lines, which is correct, but the feature also owns:
- Aiur.Config.Schema.Rtk in agent.ex:87-109, plus the embeds_one line (274) and the cast_embed line (379).
- About 95 lines in analytics_live.ex: the card template at 308-341, the assign at 365, and rtk_panel/rtk_absent/rtk_state at 396-452.
- 7 CSS lines in operator_control_center/analytics/styles.ex:67-73.
- Tests: rtk_test.exs (155 lines) and analytics_live_test.exs:1015-1143 (about 130 lines).
- The docs row at configuration.md:218.
The real total is about 370 lib lines and about 285 test lines, all removable together.

Side effect of cutting: every analytics mount currently calls Aiur.Config.settings_uncached() (a config re-read) through enabled?/0, and that goes away.

If rtk comes back later, it is an operator's host-level install (`rtk init -g`), not something Aiur needs to own.
